item.title: Heavy Quark-antiquark Systems in a Galilean Covariant MIT Bag Model
item.description: arXiv:2611.28160v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work presents a Galilean covariant extension of the MIT bag model to describe heavy quark-antiquark systems within a non-relativistic framework. Using a 5-dimensional formulation of Galilean covariance, a Dirac-like equation governing quark dynamics inside a confining bag is constructed, and the corresponding boundary conditions are derived. Analytical solutions for the spinor wavefunctions and eigenfrequencies are obtained. Numerical results show some agreement with experimental masses and hyperfine splittings for heavy mesons, particularly charmonium and bottomonium states. However, the approach is less reliable for light-quark systems, indicating the limitations of the non-relativistic approximation.
item.dc:creator: G. X. A. Petronilo, M. V. T. Machado, R. R. Luz, A. E. Santana

item.title: Revealing Dark Matter in the Dark-Electron Rate of Xenon Detectors
item.description: arXiv:2611.28211v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: There is high interest in improving experimental sensitivity to sub-GeV dark matter (DM) that scatters with electrons, as compelling theoretical models seem within reach. At the lowest DM masses, most of the expected signal lies in the single-electron regime, but so do large backgrounds. Xenon experiments therefore either do not yet search there at all or, as in XENONnT, apply cuts so severe that only $\sim$$10^{-4}$ of the exposure is retained, with sensitivity set by the criterion $S \lesssim B$, where those are the signal and background counts. We advocate that xenon detectors instead utilize most of their dark-electron rate (i.e., the total raw electron hit rate) and perform an annual-modulation search, for which the sensitivity scales as $S \lesssim \sqrt{B}$. Modern DAQs already record this rate, continuously in triggerless systems such as the XENONnT and PandaX-4T DAQs, and within trigger windows in LZ, so no new hardware is required. Using measured dark-electron rates, we estimate the sensitivity of XENONnT, LZ, PandaX-4T, PandaX-xT, and XLZD. We find that dramatic gains in sensitivity are possible, motivating new analyses of present and future xenon data.
item.dc:creator: Lillian Santos-Olmsted, Rebecca K. Leane, Carlos Blanco, John F. Beacom

item.title: Vector boson scattering in composite Higgs models
item.description: arXiv:2611.28214v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vector boson scattering is a powerful tool to test the mechanism of electroweak symmetry breaking. We focus on Composite Higgs models with an underlying fermionic description and assume that only one pseudo Nambu-Goldstone boson contributes to electroweak symmetry breaking, which we identify as the Higgs state of the Standard Model. In these scenarios, LHC data imply lower bounds on the predicted resonances below 2 TeV depending on the scenario. Using $WZjj$ production as a benchmark, we demonstrate that the tails of various distributions nevertheless show significant deviations from Standard Model predictions. This holds in particular for the case of longitudinally polarised vector bosons.
item.dc:creator: Rosy Caliri, Manuel Kunkel, Werner Porod

item.title: Unveiling the low- and high-energy frontier: a simultaneous SMEFT-PDF fit with parity violation
item.description: arXiv:2611.28216v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a comprehensive global analysis of Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT) operators utilising a diverse set of high- and low-energy experimental probes. By systematically matching the SMEFT to the Low-Energy Effective Field Theory (LEFT), we incorporate parity-violating observables into a global fit of 15 independent Wilson coefficients. This low-energy dataset, comprising parity-violation observables, neutron and nuclear $\beta$-decays, as well as leptonic and semileptonic kaon and pion decays, is combined with high-energy measurements including high-invariant-mass Drell-Yan data in both neutral- and charged-current channels, with the latter included for the first time, Higgs boson measurements, Electroweak Precision Observables (EWPOs) from LEP, and diboson production at LEP and the LHC. Crucially, this framework features a simultaneous fit of both the proton Parton Distribution Functions (PDFs) and the SMEFT Wilson coefficients using the public {\tt SIMUnet} framework. We quantify the direct interplay between SMEFT operators and hadron structure, demonstrating the robustness of the SMEFT bounds and the relative stability of the resulting PDFs with respect to the inclusion of SMEFT effects, with only a moderate increase in their uncertainties.
item.dc:creator: Ella Cole, Tom Tong, Maria Ubiali

item.title: WIMPs as FIMPs: the Inert Doublet Model and low-temperature reheating
item.description: arXiv:2611.28217v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Weakly Interacting Massive Particles (WIMPs) are conventionally assumed to acquire their dark matter relic abundance through thermal freeze-out. However, this association relies on assumptions concerning the thermal history of the early Universe. We revisit the Inert Doublet Model (IDM), a representative WIMP framework in which dark matter interacts with the Standard Model through electroweak gauge interactions, even when its Higgs-portal coupling vanishes. We demonstrate that sufficiently low reheating temperatures can prevent chemical equilibrium, allowing a genuine WIMP to acquire its relic abundance through freeze-in rather than freeze-out. Considering both instantaneous and finite-duration reheating, we identify different production histories, including freeze-out during radiation domination, freeze-out during reheating, and freeze-in with potentially significant annihilation backreactions. These scenarios open regions of the IDM parameter space that would otherwise be excluded by dark matter overabundance. Our results demonstrate that WIMPs can behave as FIMPs, depending on the thermal history of the Universe.
item.dc:creator: Genevi\`eve B\'elanger, Nicol\'as Bernal, Andreas Goudelis, Alexander Pukhov, Thomas Reggio

item.title: Scotogenic dark matter from gauged $L_\mu+L_\tau$
item.description: arXiv:2611.28223v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we introduce the first scotogenic model based on a gauged $L_{\mu} + L_{\tau}$ symmetry whose spontaneous breaking by two units leaves a remnant matter parity $M_P$. The resulting light active neutrinos are of Majorana nature and the lightest electrically neutral state mediating the scotogenic loop is stabilized by $M_P$ and can be identified as a weakly interacting massive particle dark matter candidate. We analyze the phenomenology of a predominantly singlet-like CP-even scalar dark matter candidate and the representative regions of parameter space compatible with the observed thermal relic abundance. The $Z'$ boson is compatible with a broad range of parameters relevant for dark matter. In particular, electroweak precision constraints do not lead to significant tensions for kinetic mixing values up to $\epsilon\sim 10^{-2}$. We discuss the implications of existing searches for leptophilic gauge bosons and the conditions under which visible and invisible collider signatures become relevant.
item.dc:creator: J. Echeverria-Puentes, Sergey Kovalenko, Pablo San Martin Sartori, Carlos A. Vaquera-Araujo, Yoxara Villamizar, Jilberto Zamora Saa

item.title: TeV-Scale Leptogenesis in the Linear Seesaw Framework
item.description: arXiv:2611.28224v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The linear seesaw mechanism relates the smallness of neutrino masses to the mass splitting within a quasi-Dirac pair of heavy neutrinos, thereby providing a natural framework for realising resonant leptogenesis at low energies. We investigate this possibility within its simplest effective realisation, in which neutrino masses are mediated by a quasi-Dirac pair at the TeV scale. We estimate the generation of the baryon asymmetry in the purely flavoured and strong-washout regimes, identifying phenomenologically viable parameter regions and benchmark scenarios in which the heavy-neutrino decays are dominated either by the SM Higgs doublet or by a second, leptophilic scalar doublet responsible for neutrino mass generation. We find viable leptogenesis solutions both near and away from the resonant maximum and discuss complementary phenomenological probes of the framework.
item.dc:creator: A. E. C\'arcamo Hern\'andez, J. Echeverria-Puentes, Stephen F. King, Jos\'e W. F. Valle

item.title: Higgs-portal dark matter beyond kinetic equilibrium
item.description: arXiv:2611.28230v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We revisit the scalar, vector, and fermion Higgs-portal dark matter models in the resonant regime without assuming kinetic equilibrium during the freeze-out. We compute the relic abundance by solving the full momentum-dependent Boltzmann equation and compare the results with the standard momentum-averaged treatment. We find that the standard treatment significantly underestimates the relic abundance below the resonance, apart from the fermionic case with a purely scalar portal coupling where the difference is negligible. The deviation from the standard treatment is largest for fermionic models with pseudoscalar interactions, corresponding to factor of 10 in terms of the coupling that reproduces the correct relic abundance. For the scalar and vector cases the corresponding difference is up to a factor of 2. We confront the resulting parameter space with the latest constraints from direct and indirect detection, as well as collider experiments. We find the full momentum-dependent results systematically strengthen the direct detection constraints.
item.dc:creator: Giorgio Arcadi, Michele Benaco, Mattia Di Mauro, Sami Nurmi, Kimmo Tuominen

item.title: The Nambu--Jona-Lasinio model at isospin density in closed form: what a regularization can change
item.description: arXiv:2611.28323v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: At zero temperature, the mean-field thermodynamic potential of the two-flavour Nambu-Jona-Lasinio model at isospin chemical potential reduces to a divergent momentum integral of two quasiparticle levels. In practice this integral is cut off at momenta not far above the chemical potentials being probed. We evaluate it exactly, at an arbitrary cutoff, using the Hermite reduction. The result is an algebraic boundary term and three incomplete elliptic integrals, one of each kind. Their modulus, parameter and amplitude at the end of the path are fixed by the triangle formed by the two levels at zero momentum. The power divergences reside in the boundary term, while the remaining divergence is logarithmic: the momentum axis is an open path on an elliptic curve, and the ultraviolet is the puncture at which it ends. The closed form makes the role of regularization explicit. As the cutoff is removed, sharp and smooth cutoffs acting on the momentum alone differ only by an additive constant and by two terms that the vacuum inputs fix. The medium separation scheme reproduces the resulting potential up to an additive constant. By contrast, a cutoff applied separately to the two levels generates an isospin density below the onset of condensation and violates the Silver Blaze property. The closed form gives the state that continues the vacuum along the isospin axis without numerical momentum integration. With the same vacuum fit, a cutoff kept finite gives a visibly different state. The two differ by explicit terms that vanish only as the cutoff is removed: they are different models, not two regularizations of one.
item.dc:creator: T. G. Khunjua

item.title: Chiral and deconfinement thermodynamics of the Polyakov-quark linear sigma model with and without charm quark: an SU(3) versus SU(4) comparison
item.description: arXiv:2611.28429v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using the Polyakov-loop extended linear-sigma model (PLSM), we investigate strongly interacting matter at finite temperature and baryon density by comparing the three-flavor (u,d,s) and four-flavor (u,d,s,c) formulations on equal footing, with the aim of isolating the thermal contribution of the charm quark. The model describes chiral dynamics through explicit and spontaneous symmetry breaking and reproduces the vacuum spectra of scalar and pseudoscalar mesons. Confinement is incorporated through a logarithmic Polyakov-loop potential calibrated to the continuum lattice-QCD equation of state (EoS). Within the mean-field approximation, we calculate light-, strange-, and charm-quark condensates, the Polyakov loop, and bulk thermodynamic observables, including pressure, trace anomaly, and entropy density, over broad ranges of temperature and baryon chemical potential. We also determine the chiral and deconfinement pseudocritical boundaries and represent them as phase boundaries and three-dimensional order-parameter surfaces. After tuning the Polyakov sector to lattice-QCD pressure and trace-anomaly data, the resulting entropy density agrees with HotQCD 2+1(+1)-flavor results throughout the crossover region. At zero baryon density, the non-strange condensate melts at Tc = 210 MeV in SU(3) and 218 MeV in SU(4), with curvature parameters kappa=0.018 and 0.017. Because mc>>Tc, charm remains thermally suppressed across the crossover. After normalization to the corresponding Stefan-Boltzmann limits, the SU(3) and SU(4) EoS nearly coincide below T~2Tc. Charm mainly contributes through a higher ideal-gas limit, a gradual high-temperature tail, and the flavor ordering u,d->s->c. For all baryon chemical potentials accessible within mean-field theory, the hadron-parton transition remains a smooth crossover.

item.title: Timelike electric dipole form factors of the baryon octet: short-distance kernels and baryonic rescattering
item.description: arXiv:2611.28492v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We calculate the leading-twist contribution of quark electric dipole moments (EDMs) to the timelike form factors of the baryon octet at the $J/\psi$ mass using lattice light-cone distribution amplitudes. For a strange-quark EDM $d_s$, the short-distance $\Sigma/\Lambda$ ratio is $-0.080^{+0.037}_{-0.098}$ over the lattice input ranges. This range lies above the nonrelativistic quark-model value $-1/3$. In the meson-exchange model, kaon exchange feeds the large $\Xi$ source into the $\Sigma$ channel and makes the $\Sigma$ and $\Lambda$ form factors comparable in magnitude. The short-distance $\Lambda$ form factor is about $5\times10^{-4}d_s$. The BESIII measurement then gives $|d_s|<1.3\times10^{-15}\,e\,\mathrm{cm}$ at 95% confidence level. With rescattering at a $1\,\mathrm{GeV}$ cutoff, joint fits to projected $\Lambda$, $\Sigma^+$ and $\Xi$ sensitivities lower the $\Lambda$-only upper limits by more than 25% at BESIII and the Super Tau-Charm Facility. Renormalization-scale variation changes the projected limits by about a factor of two.
item.dc:creator: Chao-Qiang Geng, Xiang-Nan Jin, Chia-Wei Liu

item.title: Probing tensor-polarized gluon TMDs through \texorpdfstring{$J/\psi$}{J/psi} electroproduction off the deuteron
item.description: arXiv:2611.28626v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate tensor-polarized gluon transverse-momentum-dependent distributions (TMDs) in semi-inclusive $J/\psi$ electroproduction off the deuteron. At leading order in the color-octet channels of nonrelativistic QCD, we derive the cross-section contributions associated with longitudinal-longitudinal ($LL$), longitudinal-transverse ($LT$), and transverse-transverse ($TT$) tensor polarization and define ten normalized observables for unpolarized and longitudinally polarized electron beams. Using gluon TMDs obtained in a spin-1 spectator model, we study their $q_T$, $y$, $Q^2$, and collision-energy dependences. The observables involving $f_{1LL}^g$, $f_{1LT}^g+h_{1LT}^g$, and $f_{1TT}^g-h_{1TT}^{\perp g}$ depend directly on ratios of gluon TMDs. The moments involving linearly polarized gluons exhibit a common zero at $Q^2=M_\psi^2$ for the adopted long-distance matrix elements, whereas the beam-helicity-dependent sine moments probe the T-odd distributions $g_{1LT}^g$ and $g_{1TT}^g$. We present fixed-scale model estimates that neglect transverse recoil from soft radiation and quarkonium formation.
item.dc:creator: Xiupeng Xie, Zhun Lu

item.title: Strong First-Order Phase Transition in a Pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone Boson Model
item.description: arXiv:2611.28630v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a novel, calculable model for realizing strong first-order phase transitions in the early Universe, in which the phase transition occurs along a pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone boson (pNGB) direction. The model involves two scalar fields whose interactions exhibit collective symmetry breaking, protecting the pNGB potential from quadratically divergent radiative corrections induced by these interactions. This structure allows strong first-order phase transitions to be realized without severe parameter tuning while maintaining perturbative control. We investigate the finite-temperature effective potential and bubble nucleation dynamics, identifying parameter regions where strong first-order phase transitions can successfully complete. The strength and characteristic time scale of the transitions are evaluated, and the resulting gravitational-wave (GW) spectra are computed. The predicted GW signals can fall within the sensitivity ranges of planned GW experiments.
item.dc:creator: Yuichiro Nakai, Masanori Tanaka, Yaoduo Wang

item.title: Emerging Topics for Hard Probes
item.description: arXiv:2611.28688v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: These proceedings present a personal selection of emerging topics in jet and heavy-flavor physics in relativistic heavy-ion collisions, based on a plenary talk delivered at Hard Probes 2026 in Nashville (USA).

item.title: Study of the $N^*(1535)$ and $N^*(1650)$ resonances from $\pi N$ $S_{11}$ scattering data and lattice QCD spectra
item.description: arXiv:2611.28691v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate two of the lowest-lying odd-parity nucleon resonances, $N^*(1535)$ and $N^*(1650)$, within a nonperturbative Hamiltonian framework (NPHF). The coupled-channel model contains two three-quark bare states with total quark spins $1/2$ and $3/2$, together with four meson-baryon channels: $\pi N$, $\eta N$, $K\Lambda$, and $K\Sigma$. Constraints from SU(3) flavor symmetry and the bare-state spin wave functions are imposed on the bare-state-channel vertices and the channel-channel Weinberg-Tomozawa interactions. This substantially reduces the number of free parameters. We combine fits to infinite-volume $\pi N$ $S_{11}$ scattering data with finite-volume lattice QCD spectra. We use Hamiltonian eigenvectors to analyze the model-basis compositions. A contamination function then compares the resulting operator-mixing pattern with lattice correlation-matrix eigenvectors. Within the scenarios considered, both bare states and coupled-channel interactions play important roles in describing the two resonances. From our combined infinite and finite volume analysis, in contrast to conventional quark-model expectations, the spin-$1/2$ bare state is heavier than the spin-$3/2$ bare state. The contamination analysis is consistent with the associated operator assignment and with a recent analysis of the relativistic wavefunctions associated with these states. The symmetry-constrained NPHF provides a unified description of the two $S_{11}$ resonances. The combined analysis also constrains their model interpretation.
item.dc:creator: Zhi-Xuan Li, Derek B. Leinweber, Anthony W. Thomas, Jia-Jun Wu

item.title: Evolution and Prospects of Higgs Boson Searches Beyond the Standard Model
item.description: arXiv:2611.28742v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The search for Higgs bosons Beyond the Standard Model (BSM) began intensively at the Large Electron-Positron (LEP) collider (1989-2000), continued at the Tevatron (2001-2011), and entered a new era with the start of the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) in 2010. While the discovery of a Higgs boson in 2012 established the Standard Model mechanism of electroweak symmetry breaking, it also opened a wide landscape of open questions that motivate ongoing BSM Higgs searches. This review traces the evolution of these searches across experiments, highlighting both experimental techniques and underlying theoretical ideas in an accessible manner. Emphasis is placed on how different collider environments shaped search strategies and how seemingly subtle experimental effects, such as small excesses, non-standard decay topologies, or suppressed couplings, can provide insight into the possible structure of extended Higgs sectors. By connecting historical developments with current analyses and future prospects, this article aims not only to summarise results but also to provide students and newcomers with intuitive insight into how Higgs searches are designed, interpreted, and continuously refined. It illustrates how experimental challenges translate into physics opportunities, thereby inviting the next generation of researchers to contribute to one of the central questions in particle physics: whether the Higgs sector is minimal or part of a more complex structure.
item.dc:creator: Andre Sopczak

item.title: Neutral and Charged Pion Modes in Magnetized Quark Matter with Chiral Imbalance
item.description: arXiv:2611.28838v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate neutral and charged pion correlations in a two-flavor Nambu--Jona-Lasinio (NJL) model at finite temperature in the presence of a uniform magnetic field and a prescribed chiral chemical potential $\mu_5$, using the mean-field approximation and the single-channel random phase approximation (RPA). The pion masses are defined by the selected positive-energy zeros of the real parts of the corresponding inverse propagators. We demonstrate that, at zero external spatial momentum, the complete Dirac trace in the neutral channel eliminates mixed-branch contributions, thereby precluding a finite-energy Landau cut. In contrast, the charged channel allows non-diagonal Landau-level transitions and exhibits both pair-production and thermal-scattering contributions. With increasing $\mu_5$, the neutral-pion mass exhibits only a weak variation at low temperature, while the rapid decrease of the mass shifts toward higher temperatures. The charged-pion mass decreases with increasing $\mu_5$ over the selected solution segments. This behavior may help account for the lattice QCD results. At zero temperature and fixed $\mu_5$, increasing the magnetic field lowers the neutral-pion mass but raises the charged-pion mass.
item.dc:creator: Shijie Zhai, Lang Yu, Jie Mei, Mei Huang

item.title: A billion colour states: exact soft-gluon evolution beyond leading colour for many-jet QCD
item.description: arXiv:2611.29072v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a new method, and its implementation, for constructing orthogonal colour bases and computing colour factors for any process with quarks, antiquarks and gluons, and use it to compute one-loop soft-gluon evolution exactly in full colour, keeping all colour interference. Each basis vector is labelled, independently of $N_c$, by the sequence of colour representations that appear when the partons are coupled one at a time. We derive a closed formula for the norms of the basis vectors, and colour operators act only on the part of a label between the partons involved, through small tables. Basis vectors can therefore be generated and used one at a time, without listing the complete basis: norms and matrix elements of single basis vectors are obtained for $10^4$ gluons in seconds. The same locality lets the soft anomalous dimension act on colour states without being stored. This allows optimised implementations on CPUs and GPUs, with which we evolve colour states exactly for up to fourteen gluons on a single GPU and for fifteen gluons, a colour space of $827\,888\,726$ dimensions, on a single compute node. We validate the basis and the evolution against independent codes and published results for processes with few partons, the only ones for which such results are available. We then measure the accuracy of leading colour as a function of the number of partons. For exclusive jet rates with a veto on soft radiation outside the jets, at a ratio of about 14 between the hard and the veto scale, leading colour overestimates the full-colour result by a median factor of 1.3 for eight partons, 1.8 for ten and 6.6 for fourteen. Pairs of hard jets are in a colour singlet with probabilities of several per cent, which vanish at leading colour. The formal $1/N_c^2$ suppression of subleading colour therefore does not make it small for many-jet final states.
item.dc:creator: Bakar Chargeishvili

item.title: Quantifying the Impact of Galactic Dark Matter Halo Models on LZ Results
item.description: arXiv:2611.29197v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Most dark matter direct-detection limits are reported under the assumption of an isotropic, Maxwellian Standard Halo Model. However, the Milky Way's stellar halo exhibits substantial radial anisotropy, while cosmological simulations predict scale-dependent anisotropy in the dark matter velocity distribution. We investigate how departures from isotropy affect the interpretation of LZ results in two complementary regimes: background-dominated elastic-scattering searches and the recently reported 248 keV nuclear-recoil candidate, which we study using a background-free single-event approximation. For elastic scattering, we use the self-consistent isotropic, Osipkov-Merritt, axisymmetric, and triaxial halo models of Belli et al. and translate the published limits through the ratio of predicted event counts, applying a common escape-speed truncation in the Galactic frame. At WIMP masses above approximately 40 GeV, the resulting limits lie within about $\pm 30\%$ of the isotropic reference. Below approximately 15 GeV, the model envelope broadens to as much as an order of magnitude, reflecting sensitivity to the high-velocity tail. For the 248 keV event, the accessible inelastic mass splitting is likewise controlled by this tail. Some anisotropic models extend the allowed kinematic region towards splittings at which solar-neutrino constraints on a Higgsino interpretation become ineffective, although kinematic accessibility alone does not establish viability at the fixed Higgsino cross section. These results show that halo-model dependence is modest at high WIMP masses but becomes essential near kinematic thresholds.
item.dc:creator: Jialiang Shao, Andrea Addazi, Xinran Wang, Guanwen Fang, Yi-Fu Cai

item.title: Infrared divergences in the $\mathcal{O}(\alpha_s v^2)$ corrections to exclusive $J/\psi$ photoproduction
item.description: arXiv:2611.29272v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the infrared structure of exclusive $J/\psi$ photoproduction, $\gamma p\to J/\psi p$, up to relative order $\alpha_s v^2$ within the frameworks of generalized parton distribution (GPD) and nonrelativistic QCD (NRQCD) factorization. By analyzing the singular loop-momentum regions, we extract the soft and collinear singular terms and identify residual infrared poles at relative order $\alpha_s v^2$ after QCD renormalization, collinear factorization into the GPDs, and NRQCD matching. These poles originate from incomplete cancellation of soft-gluon exchange between the heavy-quark pair and the target-collinear partons. We verify the pole coefficients through a complete one-loop calculation. We examine the local NRQCD operator basis and find no additional independent vacuum-to-$J/\psi$ matrix element that can absorb these poles. These findings motivate further investigation of factorization in exclusive $J/\psi$ photoproduction.
item.dc:creator: Zi-Qiang Chen, Long-Bin Chen

item.title: Neutron lifetime puzzle and Dicke coherence in spontaneous decays
item.description: arXiv:2611.29328v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The long-standing discrepancy between beam and bottle measurements of the free-neutron lifetime---known as the neutron lifetime puzzle---remains an open anomaly in nuclear and particle physics. Here, we investigate whether collective quantum synchronization via macroscopic Dicke superradiance can influence free-neutron decay or mediate the relaxation of hypothetical excited neutron states. We show that superradiance is fundamentally obstructed in standard three-body weak beta decay by continuous final-state phase space and fermionic antisymmetrization, and remains inactive in terrestrial ultracold neutron traps due to low particle densities, even within the Koch--Hummel excited-neutron model. Extending this analysis to the primordial plasma prior to Big Bang nucleosynthesis, we demonstrate that rapid $e^\pm$ collisional dephasing and intense thermal photon backgrounds prevent a superradiant purge and instead enforce thermal detailed balance. Consequently, across the entire parameter space unconstrained by terrestrial experiments, an excited neutron state inevitably thermalizes before weak freeze-out, increasing the effective neutron statistical weight and severely overproducing primordial $^4\text{He}$, thereby excluding the standard realization of the Koch--Hummel hypothesis.
item.dc:creator: Z. K. Silagadze

item.title: Diffractive $D^0$ photoproduction in ultraperipheral collisions at the LHC
item.description: arXiv:2611.29527v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We compute the cross section for coherent diffractive $D^0$ photoproduction in ultraperipheral lead-lead and proton-lead collisions (UPCs) at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) within the Color Glass Condensate (CGC) effective field theory. We include both the exclusive production of a charm-anticharm pair and diffractive production with an additional semi-hard gluon, described in diffractive transverse-momentum-dependent (TMD) factorization. We show that the diffractive channel, although suppressed by the strong coupling, dominates at large transverse momentum, where the exclusive channel is suppressed by color transparency. Furthermore, we quantify nuclear effects at the parton level with a nuclear modification factor $R_{pA}$ at fixed photon energy, which shows a mild suppression for the diffractive channel and an enhancement growing with transverse momentum up to about a factor of 2 for the exclusive one. We also use the diffractive cross section to correct our inclusive $D^0$ predictions to the CMS event selection, which requires the target nucleus to break up, and compare them with the data. Finally, we provide predictions for inclusive $D^0$ photoproduction in proton-lead UPCs.
item.dc:creator: Paul Caucal, Patricia Gimeno-Estivill, Tuomas Lappi, Farid Salazar

item.title: Pseudoscalar Yukawa Preheating via Effective Action Approach
item.description: arXiv:2611.29659v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we investigate helicity-dependent fermion production driven by a pseudoscalar Yukawa interaction within the one-loop effective action framework. By integrating out the fermionic fields and employing the Schwinger proper time representation, we derive an analytical expression for the fermion pair production probability near each zero crossing of the oscillating inflaton field. We further introduce a helicity transfer matrix to describe the evolution of fermionic modes through successive non-adiabatic production events. For an undamped inflaton background, the temporal symmetry around successive zero crossings leads to the cancellation of helicity-mixing contributions after an even number of events, preventing the accumulation of helicity asymmetry. We then extend the analysis to a damped oscillatory background, in which the decreasing inflaton amplitude breaks this temporal symmetry and modifies the transfer matrix at each crossing. The resulting non-commuting transfer matrices produce a persistent helical spectrum, as demonstrated by the probabilities as a function of momentum obtained after successive scattering events. A comparison with scalar Yukawa preheating further confirms the role of helicity mixing in generating the helical asymmetry induced by pseudoscalar mechanism. These results establish an effective action framework for studying helicity asymmetry during fermionic preheating and provide insight into the influence of the inflaton's dynamical evolution on particle production.
item.dc:creator: Xi-Bin Li, De-Tian Zhao, Ke Fu, Jun-Yang Jiao

item.title: Two-loop correction to the complex-bion amplitude in a quasi-exactly solvable sextic oscillator
item.description: arXiv:2611.29701v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this study, a quasi-exactly solvable sextic potential is analyzed by two diagrammatic calculations. At positive coupling, factorization fixes the ground-state energy $E_0$ exactly and forces every perturbative coefficient to vanish. Using only Feynman diagrams, we verify this cancellation explicitly through third order. After continuation to negative coupling, the formal zero mode becomes nonnormalizable. A real instanton remains, but its one-instanton contribution to \(E_0\) vanishes. In particular, the leading shift in energy arises from a complex neutral bion. Taking an exact constrained family, we calculate its local median amplitude through two loops. The direct diagrammatic sum gives $c_{\rm 2L}^{\rm diag}=-0.750000(5)$, in excellent agreement with the exact-WKB value $-3/4$.
item.dc:creator: Adrian M. Escobar-Ruiz

item.title: Magic Production and the Fundamental Forces of Nature
item.description: arXiv:2611.29717v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum magic is a resource for universal quantum computation and may also provide a probe of fundamental interactions. We study its production in forward scattering of two distinct Standard Model fermions in the chirality basis. In the single-mediator-exchange approximation, magic production vanishes for gluon, photon, W-boson, Higgs-boson, and graviton exchange. For Z-boson exchange in purely leptonic scattering, it also vanishes at $\sin^2\theta_W = 1/4$, close to the phenomenological value. By contrast, Z-boson exchange involving elementary quarks generally produces nonzero magic. These patterns raise the question of whether the construction of the fundamental forces encodes, at least in some channels, a tendency to suppress magic production.
item.dc:creator: Jiunn-Wei Chen, Yu-Hao Li

item.title: Few-gluon interactions in high-energy collisions
item.description: arXiv:2611.29777v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A conventional narrative developed for high energy heavy ion collisions prior to the RHIC program assumed hadron production dominated by hot and dense QGP formation, expansion and freezeout. Proposed diagnostics included detection of elliptic and radial flows via correlation and spectrum analysis and jet quenching in a dense medium via rescaled spectrum ratios. The validity of that narrative has come into question in recent years with detection of similar features in data from small collision systems. In response, several recent observations hint at a strongly modified narrative. Study of p-Pb spectra has revealed that the Glauber Monte Carlo estimation of A-B collision geometry is quite misleading. Collision geometry should instead be inferred by inverting ensemble-mean $\bar p_t$ data. A method has been developed to transform $v_2(p_t)$ data to quadrupole spectra $\bar \rho_2(p_t)$ that provide new insights into the true correlation mechanism. Accurate $p_t$-integrated $v_2$ vs $n_{ch}$ measurements for p-p collisions reveal a cubic trend suggesting a three-gluon interaction as the true mechanism. The p-p $v_2(n_{ch})$ trend has been generalized to describe all A-B collision systems in common in terms of an extensive measure $V_2^2 \equiv \bar \rho_0^2 v_2^2$ (number of correlated pairs). A similar program has been applied to jet-related contributions to spectra and angular correlations with a comparable result, a quadratic trend on $n_{ch}$ as expected for two-gluon interactions. Those new results suggest that the relevant data features actually represent multipole (color dipole and quadrupole) radiation from few-gluon interactions within a low-density system.
item.dc:creator: Thomas A. Trainor

item.title: Compactification and non-zero density in (2+1)-dimensional four-fermion model
item.description: arXiv:2611.29823v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The phase diagram of (2+1)-dimensional NJL type model has been studied with one compact dimension. The effect of compactification and fermion density on the chiral symmetry breaking is considered for periodic boundary conditions.
item.dc:creator: K. G. Klimenko, A. N. Kozhakin, R. N. Zhokhov

item.title: Flavor-resolved screening length of a moving quarkonium in a lattice-calibrated holographic QCD plasma
item.description: arXiv:2611.29953v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We compute the screening length \(L_s\) of a moving heavy quark-antiquark pair in a lattice-calibrated Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton background for pure-glue, two-flavor, and \(2+1\)-flavor matter. Parallel and perpendicular orientations are considered at finite temperature, baryon chemical potential, and rapidity. \(L_s\) decreases monotonically with \(T\) and \(\eta\) in every flavor sector, and for the flavored systems also with \(\mu\). The perpendicular screening length is systematically smaller than the parallel one. At zero density and \(T=0.3\ \mathrm{GeV}\), the ordering \(L_s^{(N_f=0)}>L_s^{(N_f=2)}>L_s^{(N_f=2+1)}\) holds in this calibration, and a lattice check of the static flavor dependence is proposed. At finite density the two-flavor and \(2+1\)-flavor curves cross along a line in the \(T\)-\(\mu\) plane; below the line \(L_s^{(N_f=2)}>L_s^{(N_f=2+1)}\), while above it the ordering reverses. The crossing follows from the competition between the two-flavor crossover temperature and the density coupling, and its location depends on the fitted parameters. These results provide a flavor-resolved reference for moving quarkonium screening in the baryon-rich regime probed by beam energy scans.
item.dc:creator: Huwei Zhu, Zi-qiang Zhang

item.title: Plasma-enabled magnet-free LSW search for eV-scale axions with laser-stimulated regeneration
item.description: arXiv:2611.30098v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In conventional light-shining-through-a-wall (LSW) experiments, strong magnetic fields mediate the conversion of photons into axions and their subsequent reconversion into photons. At eV-scale axion masses, however, photon--axion phase mismatch causes these conversions to lose coherence, substantially reducing the experimental sensitivity. We propose a magnet-free LSW scheme that addresses this limitation via plasma-based axion generation and laser-stimulated regeneration. At low laser intensity, a two-color dispersion-matched source generates axions in a narrow mass range set by the plasma dispersion. At relativistic laser intensity, a single-pulse plasma-broadened source generates axions over a broad mass range, as shown by particle-in-cell simulations. The Fourier spectrum of the source term $\mathbf{E}\cdot\mathbf{B}$ broadens around the laser branch, consistent with mixing between the laser and low-frequency plasma waves. For axion detection behind the wall, a counter-propagating laser stimulates axion decay into a detectable signal photon and a second photon emitted into the laser mode, with the laser frequency chosen to satisfy phase matching. For representative parameters, the requirement of at least one regenerated photon yields projected upper limits on the axion-photon coupling on the order $10^{-7}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$ over $m_a=0.1$--$1\,\mathrm{eV}$.
item.dc:creator: Xiangyan An, Min Chen, Yipeng Wu, Boyuan Li, Wenchao Yan, Peng Yuan, Binbin Yan, Feng Liu, Zhengming Sheng, Jie Zhang

item.title: Superheavy gravitational dark matter from runaway bubble collisions
item.description: arXiv:2611.30113v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A stable particle that couples only through gravity is pair-produced in collisions of runaway bubble walls by graviton exchange. For a transition of duration $1/\beta$, a Dirac fermion reaches the yield $Y_X\simeq6.8\times10^{-3}(H/\beta)(T_{\rm reh}/M_{\rm P})^3$, where $H$ is the Hubble rate of the vacuum energy, $T_{\rm reh}$ the reheating temperature and $M_{\rm P}$ the reduced Planck mass. The yield is flat up to masses near $(H/\beta)M_{\rm P}/\nu^2$, where $\nu$ of order one sets the wall-field excursion. Gravity alone then gives dark matter up to about $10^{17}$~GeV at reheating temperatures far below its mass, where freeze-in fails.
item.dc:creator: Cheng-Wei Chiang, Van Que Tran

item.title: Quark and gluon gravitational form factors of the nucleon at next-to-leading order
item.description: arXiv:2611.30124v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We compute the quark and gluon gravitational form factors $A$, $J$ and $D$ of the nucleon in three-point QCD sum rules at next-to-leading order in $\alpha_s$ for the quark and gluon energy-momentum tensors (EMT), treating both at the same order in the $\overline{\rm MS}$ scheme. The nucleon EMT also tests the method, showing where the sum rules are reliable and why. Protected estimators of $D$ and of the trace form factor $\bar c$ require antisymmetric Borel moments, since none with equal Borel masses alone is protected. The $\mathcal{O}(\alpha_s)$ corrections reduce $A_{\rm tot}$ by $32$--$40\%$, $J_{\rm tot}$ by $22$--$27\%$ and $|D_{\rm tot}|$ by $21$--$27\%$, since the perturbative share of the two-point function is much larger. The total form factors agree with lattice QCD for $1\le Q^2\le2.5$~GeV$^2$. At $Q^2=1.5$~GeV$^2$, $A_{\rm tot}=0.337\pm0.113$, $J_{\rm tot}=0.206\pm0.100$ and $D_{\rm tot}=-0.206\pm0.121$. $D$ is the most reliable result: its correlator is mostly perturbative, and its quark and gluon parts agree with the lattice. In $A$ and $J$, a local gluon-condensate term that does not fall with $Q^2$ is the largest, and their gluon shares are well below the lattice, possibly because the gluon EMT couples at this order only through gluon exchange and the condensate. A working region exists only near $\beta=1$, and the constant part of transitions cannot be separated within the Borel windows. The individual conservation identities deviate at one point by two standard deviations, consistent with a missing finite term in the $g_{\mu\nu}$ structure, and $\bar c$ is therefore given at leading order with condensates.
item.dc:creator: Ula\c{s} \"{O}zdem

item.title: Effect of dark matter and scalar-cut potential on the macroscopic properties of neutron stars: A chiral quark mean field approach
item.description: arXiv:2611.30434v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the effects of fermionic dark matter (DM) and scalar-cut potential ($U_{\text{cut}}(\phi)$) on the equation of state (EOS) and macroscopic properties of neutron stars. The baryonic matter consists of neutrons, protons, electrons, and muons under the $\beta$-equilibrium and is described within the chiral SU(3) quark mean-field (CQMF) model. In this framework, quarks are confined within baryons, whose properties are modified through the exchange of scalar fields $\sigma$, $\zeta$, and $\delta$, and vector fields $\omega$ and $\rho$. The DM is modelled as a self-interacting fermionic fluid with scalar $\varphi_D$ and vector $V_D^\mu$ mediators. The baryonic and DM fluids interact only through gravity and are treated within a two-fluid Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff formalism. We examine the resulting mass-radius relation and tidal deformability, along with the gravitational redshift, to investigate the effects of DM on neutron star structure and observable properties. The inclusion of $U_{\text{cut}}(\phi)$ stiffens the EOS, whereas increasing the DM fraction generally softens the EOS and modifies the mass-radius relation, tidal deformability, and gravitational redshift. The magnitude and nature of these modifications depend on the DM particle mass and mediator interactions, which determine whether the resulting configurations exhibit compact DM cores or extended DM halos.
item.dc:creator: Hrishika P, Arvind Kumar

item.title: Pion scattering in finite volume within the Inverse Amplitude Method: Extension to moving frames
item.description: arXiv:2611.30475v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the leading exponentially suppressed finite-volume corrections to $\pi\pi$ scattering near threshold in moving frames. Using the one-loop Inverse Amplitude Method (IAM), we compute the $I=0$ and $I=2$ amplitudes in a box with total momentum $\vec P=2\pi\vec d/L$, including the left-hand cut and the $t$-, $u$-channel and tadpole contributions neglected in L\"uscher's quantization condition. We derive the resulting correction to the near-threshold energy levels and measure its size relative to the L\"uscher term. We find that it becomes comparable to the latter for $m_\pi L\lesssim 1.5$--$1.7$ at rest, and that it is larger in moving frames, reaching $m_\pi L\lesssim 2.8$ for $\vec d=[002]$. The corrections become negligible only for $m_\pi L\gtrsim 5$.
item.dc:creator: Juli\'an A. S\'anchez, Raquel Molina, \'Angel G\'omez Nicola

item.title: Chiral crossover responses in a magnetic field: Finite-$\mu_5$ matching in the NJL model
item.description: arXiv:2611.30535v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate how independent information at finite chiral chemical potential $\mu_5$ constrains pseudocritical-temperature responses in the Nambu-Jona-Lasinio model under a magnetic field. Vacuum calibration alone leaves the coefficient $c_r$ of the additional interaction $\delta\Omega_r=c_r\mu_5^2(M-m_0)^2$ undetermined. We compare soft-cutoff (SC) and Pauli-Villars (PV) vacuum regularizations, each combined with the direct treatment (D) or the magnetic finite-difference scheme (MFDS). The reference SC and PV treatments exhibit opposite finite-$\mu_5$ responses already at $eB=0$. Matching the $eB=0$ scalar-susceptibility peak-temperature ratio predicted by unitarized chiral perturbation theory gives $c_{\mathrm{SC}}=-0.07112$ and $c_{\mathrm{PV}}=0.22479$. Holding these coefficients fixed at $eB=0.1,0.2,0.4$ GeV$^2$ reduces the four-treatment spread of the normalized finite-$\mu_5$-induced mass-inflection temperature change by factors of approximately $7.5$-$15.3$ at $\mu_5=0.15$ GeV and $18.1$-$32.6$ at $\mu_5=0.30$ GeV. For the distinct scalar-susceptibility peak-temperature ratio at $\mu_5=0.15$ GeV, the spread decreases by factors of approximately $74$, $27$, and $14$ at the same magnetic fields, respectively. The reduction in regularization-dependent finite-$\mu_5$ responses thus persists at the sampled nonzero magnetic fields without further matching.
item.dc:creator: Jingyi Chao

item.title: Towards a Global CE$\nu$NS Picture
item.description: arXiv:2611.30638v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a general framework for extracting and interpreting the Coherent Elastic Neutrino-Nucleus Scattering (CE$\nu$NS) differential cross-section from experimental data. A generalized parametric basis, constructed from common kinematic terms recurring in generalized neutrino interaction models, is employed to numerically constrain the shape and normalization of the observed CE$\nu$NS response. The framework was applied to the COHERENT CsI and liquid argon datasets using Bayesian inference, yielding normalization constraints comparable to those reported by the Collaboration while providing additional constraints on the correlated spectral shape. A combined analysis was also performed, exploiting the complementary sensitivities of the two datasets to constrain features of the differential cross-section that are less accessible to either dataset individually. The framework has been implemented in the open-source Julia package Newtrinos.jl, which supports modular forward modeling, parallel computation, and automatic differentiation.
item.dc:creator: Heerak Banerjee, Philipp Eller

item.title: Construction of a conserved energy-momentum tensor of the Skyrmion coupled to additional dynamical degrees in the large-$N_c$ expansion
item.description: arXiv:2611.30698v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We formulate an order-by-order construction of a conserved energy-momentum tensor (EMT) in the large-$N_c$ expansion of the model where the Skyrmion is coupled to additional dynamical fields. We show that, expanding the equations of motion and the EMT in powers of $1/N_c$, the inclusion of the backreaction to the Skyrmion from the additional fields is essential for achieving the conservation law of the EMT, which is contrasted with the fixed-background approximation where the effects of backreaction are neglected. We apply the construction to the model for hyperons based on the Callan-Klebanov bound-state approach, where the antikaon is bound to the Skyrmion, to obtain the EMT up to next-to-leading order of the $1/N_c$ expansion. We explicitly show that the divergence of the EMT from the backreaction for the Skyrmion exactly cancels that of the kaon to achieve the conservation of the total EMT. We find that the conserved EMT gives a negative hyperon D-term whose magnitude is smaller than that of the nucleon D-term and radii of gravitational form factors for the hyperon smaller than those for the nucleon, which implies that the hyperon is more compact than the nucleon.
item.dc:creator: Mitsuru Tanaka, Yasuhiro Yamaguchi, Masayasu Harada

item.title: Exact analytic solutions for the $n=1$ chameleon field in planar systems with an arbitrary number of uniform layers
item.description: arXiv:2611.30712v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scalar fields have long been investigated as a potential dark energy candidate. Of these models, screened scalar fields like the chameleon have received interest due to their ability to avoid observational constraints. However, the non-linear nature of these models has led to there being only a small number of exact analytic solutions within the literature. In this work, we present exact analytic solutions for the $n=1$ chameleon model in a planar system consisting of $N$ discrete regions of uniform density. We compare these to the relevant approximate solutions within the literature. We also use our solutions to forecast constraints from CANNEX, a recent experiment devised to measure Casimir forces and detect hypothetical fifth forces. Unlike in previous works, we consider the full fifteen-layered setup of CANNEX, as opposed to treating the plate and wall as single uniform objects. Doing so revealed an increase in the induced chameleon pressure of up to $\sim 7 \%$. However, the resulting gain is insufficient to probe new regions of parameter space at the projected sensitivities.
item.dc:creator: Chad Briddon, Mario Pitschmann

item.title: A general formalism for electromagnetic production of two mesons on the nucleon
item.description: arXiv:2611.30755v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a general formalism for the electromagnetic production of two mesons on the nucleon, $\gamma_{\rm v}N\to\Phi_1\Phi_2B$, that can be used in single-channel as well as coupled-channel analyses over a wide range of energies. In the spirit of the decomposition introduced by Berends et al. for single-meson electroproduction, the hadronic current is expanded in a set of 16 gauge- and Lorentz-invariant matrices, four of which vanish for real photons. The corresponding Lorentz-invariant (Dirac) amplitudes can be obtained from any reaction model and are mapped onto 16 CGLN-like Pauli amplitudes, from which the five-fold differential cross section and its transverse, longitudinal, and interference response functions follow directly. Although these matrices are not all linearly independent, they follow directly from the covariant decomposition of the current, so the amplitudes can be read off from the Feynman diagrams and the observables take a simpler, more symmetric form. As a first application, we calculate the $\gamma p\to\pi^0\pi^0p$ and $\gamma p\to\pi^+\pi^0n$ reactions near threshold from tree-level nucleon Born terms. This example shows explicitly how the Dirac amplitudes are read off from Feynman diagrams and how gauge invariance, which is violated by the individual diagrams, is restored in the total amplitude and preserved when hadronic form factors are included. The formalism thus provides a versatile basis for future theoretical and phenomenological studies of double-meson photo- and electroproduction. A more complete abstract is provided in the paper.
item.dc:creator: Reddy Malik Priandika, Samson Clymton, Terry Mart

item.title: Fate of Vainshtein Screening for UV/IR Mixing with a $P(X)$ Higgs Classicalizer
item.description: arXiv:2611.30764v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Classicalization is a non-Wilsonian framework in which an effective field theory self-completes above its strong-coupling scale by generating semiclassical objects that decay into many soft quanta, thereby realizing ultraviolet-infrared mixing. A key requirement of this mechanism is that the force carrier be lighter than the strong-coupling scale. A natural application would be to embed classicalization in the electroweak Higgs sector to address the little hierarchy problem. In this work, we investigate whether Higgs classicalization can occur within the $P(X)$ class of gauged k-essence and k-chameleon models. For classicalization to occur, the theory must support Vainshtein screening around a sharply localized source. Our results show that it fails to do so, even when one attempts to engineer a symbiosis with chameleon screening through a gauge kinetic function, owing to a strong-coupling breakdown inside the screening region. These $P(X)$ theories therefore fail to provide a suitable framework for Higgs classicalization. Nevertheless, we emphasize that our results, obtained for a specific class of models, should not be interpreted as a no-go theorem for Higgs classicalization.
item.dc:creator: El\'eana Berteaux, Florian Nortier

item.title: Light on GeV-scale seesaw
item.description: arXiv:2611.30780v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The next generation of beam-dump and accelerator-neutrino experiments will probe GeV-scale sterile neutrinos with unprecedented sensitivity. However, the tiny active-sterile mixing predicted by the minimal seesaw mechanism is expected to remain out of reach. Oscillation data require at least two sterile neutrinos, $N_1$ and $N_2$, which may couple to the photon through a transition dipole. Such a coupling can radically change the picture, both by strongly enhancing sterile-neutrino production and by opening new decay channels. We identify charged-lepton pairs produced by an off-shell photon as the most promising experimental signature. We show that the seesaw band can be probed by the T2K near detector for sterile-neutrino masses $m_N\lesssim 500$ MeV, and by SHiP for $m_N\lesssim 5$ GeV. For a sufficiently large dipole, $d\gtrsim (10~\mathrm{TeV})^{-1}$, SHiP can selectively measure decay channels that require nonzero active-sterile mixing. This would give rise to a distinctive hierarchy of signatures, providing a direct test of the seesaw mechanism.
item.dc:creator: Enrico Bertuzzo, Michele Frigerio, Salvador Urrea

item.title: Fermionic dark linear seesaw with an anomalous Majoron
item.description: arXiv:2611.30799v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a minimal fermionic realisation of the $\textit{dark}$ linear seesaw with spontaneous breaking of lepton number. The small lepton-number-violating parameter responsible for linear-seesaw neutrino masses is generated radiatively by a $\textit{dark}$ sector consisting of a singlet and a doublet fermion, together with scalar singlets. The global U(1)$_L$ symmetry is broken to a residual $\mathcal{Z}_2$ under which the $\textit{dark}$ sector is odd. This breaking yields a Majoron $J$ and makes the lightest $\textit{dark}$ particle stable. The charged $\textit{dark}$ fermion acquires its mass solely from U(1)$_L$ breaking and thus induces an anomalous Majoron coupling to photons. Current bounds on this coupling exclude a massless Majoron for TeV-scale U(1)$_L$ breaking. We add a linear term that breaks lepton number softly and gives the Majoron a GeV-scale mass. Such a Majoron decays into two photons and can be probed at beam-dump experiments. We study the dark matter phenomenology, focusing on the case where the stable particle is a fermionic weakly interacting massive particle. We analyse how the framework can be tested through charged-lepton flavour-violating decays such as $\mu \to e\gamma$, which receive contributions from both the $\textit{dark}$ and the seesaw sectors. Moreover, both sectors enhance the Majoron couplings to charged leptons, so that the Majoron-emitting decays $\tau \to \ell J$ ($\ell = e,\mu$) typically exceed $\tau \to \ell\gamma$ by orders of magnitude and can probe parameter space beyond the reach of $\mu \to e\gamma$.
item.dc:creator: A. Batra, H. B. C\^amara, F. R. Joaquim

item.title: Diffractive Photoproduction of High $p_T$ Photons in Ultraperipheral Collisions at the LHC
item.description: arXiv:2611.30966v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate diffractive photoproduction of large-transverse-momentum photons in ultraperipheral collisions at the LHC, considering different collision systems and alternative descriptions of the BFKL Pomeron. We estimate cross sections and differential distributions including NLO corrections to the BFKL characteristic function and assess the prospects for measuring this process in ultraperipheral pp, pPb, and PbPb collisions. We find that the cross sections are sizable, and that future measurements in this channel can help constrain BFKL dynamics and improve our understanding of high-energy QCD.
item.dc:creator: Jo\~ao V. Bulh\~oes, Victor P. Goncalves

item.title: Lorentz symmetry in self-supervised representation learning
item.description: arXiv:2611.31011v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Self-supervised learning (SSL) and explicit physical inductive biases have driven major advances in jet tagging, yet they are typically pursued along separate tracks. In this work, we unify both paradigms by integrating the Lorentz-equivariant Geometric Algebra Transformer slim (L-GATr-slim) architecture with the LeJEPA framework for representation learning. Pre-training on 100 million jets from the JetClass dataset, we optimize towards a latent space, which is invariant across physics-motivated jet augmentations. We demonstrate that enforcing Lorentz symmetry in the latent space is critical for representation quality and that this can be achieved either architecturally or learned via kinematic augmentations. With a standard non-invariant Transformer backbone, LeJEPA outperforms established autoregressive, masked particle modelling, and self-distillation baselines in linear- and MLP-probe accuracy, with L-GATr-slim providing further complementary gains. Across downstream benchmarks, our pre-trained models consistently outperform baselines trained from scratch or through different pre-training objectives.
item.dc:creator: Andreas Hermansen, Tobias Golling, Slava Voloshynovskiy

item.title: Kaon-pair production with NNLO effects
item.description: arXiv:2611.31080v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Monte Carlo framework McMule has been extended to support the processes $e^+\,e^-\to K^+\,K^-$ and $e^+\,e^-\to K^0\,\bar{K}^0$. Our results include NNLO initial-state QED corrections together with NLO mixed corrections. The latter are evaluated in the FsQED approach, using disperon QED. The implementation is fully differential and can be used with any kaon form factor. We present the total cross section for energies relevant to the CMD-3 experiment and observe very large corrections. For $e^+\,e^-\to K^+\,K^-$ we also present selected differential observables for energies around the $\phi(1020)$ resonance.
item.dc:creator: Yizhou Fang, Sophie Kollatzsch, Adrian Signer

item.title: A proposal for an LHC search for baryon number violation in complementarity with trilepton nucleon decay searches
item.description: arXiv:2611.31142v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the compatibility of existing limits on trilepton nucleon decay by the Super-Kamiokande (Super-K) experiment with Baryon Number Violation (BNV) at the TeV scale and motivate a dedicated search using existing data at the LHC. Working within an effective field theory framework, we derive model-independent constraints on higher-dimensional operators associated with $B - L/3$ conserving texture of BNV. We demonstrate that existing Super-K limits on loop-level trilepton nucleon decay provide significantly stronger constraints compared to tree-level charm-baryon decays induced by these operators. These constraints translate into bounds of $O(1-30)$ TeV on the BNV scale, leaving open the possibility of an LHC search for $B - L/3$ type BNV. Motivated by this complementarity, we investigate the collider phenomenology of a representative UV completion featuring an $s$-channel diquark resonance that decays into a leptoquark--dilepton pair, producing a distinctive final state containing an anti-top quark, two charged anti-leptons, and missing transverse energy. Our results indicate that, although same-sign dilepton searches by ATLAS and CMS already place indirect constraints on this model, a dedicated analysis based on the selection cuts we develop significantly extends the reach for our chosen benchmarks. In particular, using only Run 2 data, we demonstrate complementary reach to limits on trilepton nucleon decay searches set by the Super-K experiment and to the projected reach of Hyper-Kamiokande. The selection cuts are applicable beyond our representative model.
item.dc:creator: Amit Bhoonah, Francis M. Burk, Da Liu, Tong Ou, Deepak Sathyan

item.title: New analytic constraints for the soft anomalous dimension bootstrap at three loops
item.description: arXiv:2611.31168v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The soft anomalous dimension governs the universal long-distance singularities of gauge theory amplitudes. It exhibits a highly constrained analytic structure and has been shown to be amenable to bootstrap methods. In this paper we revisit the relation between unitarity cuts and sequential discontinuities of Feynman integrals and use it to derive new constraints on the soft anomalous dimension. At three loops, we show that certain sequential discontinuities in non-overlapping two-particle channels vanish for every web contributing to the quadrupole function that correlates four coloured partons. These constraints hold for arbitrary parton masses, and we explicitly verify them for the known massless and one-mass cases. We then demonstrate their constraining power by substantially strengthening the massless bootstrap and carrying out the first bootstrap construction of the one-mass quadrupole function. The new constraints are largely complementary to those arising from the absence of unphysical branch points, symmetries, and collinear and Regge limits. With their help, we determine each quadrupole function within the assumed function space up to a single coefficient, which we fix by matching to existing diagrammatic results. These results open the way to bootstrapping the three-loop soft anomalous dimension for amplitudes with several massive partons.
item.dc:creator: Einan Gardi, Luke Lippstreu, Andrew J. McLeod, Laura Walsh, Zehao Zhu, Enrico Zunino

item.title: Photomeson-threshold origin of the TeV break in astrophysical neutrinos: Spectrum, flavor, resolved sources, and the ultrahigh-energy landscape
item.description:
arXiv:2611.28037v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: IceCube observes a break near 30 TeV in the diffuse astrophysical neutrino spectrum. We interpret it as the photomeson ($p\gamma$) threshold. Accelerated protons interact with the soft x rays of accreting black holes through the $\Delta(1232)$ resonance. One kinematic relation sets the break energy from the target field's lowest photon energy, the seed scale $\varepsilon_0$. The measured break fixes $\varepsilon_0\simeq0.13$ keV and supplies the low-energy suppression no sum of falling power laws can produce. Building on the $\Delta(1232)$ identification of Khatee Zathul, Fang, Halzen, and Hooper and the single-source-class photo-pion fit of Winter, Fiorillo, and Buson, we give closed-form relations that invert the four broken-power-law parameters to the source physics with no remaining freedom, namely, $\gamma_2=s$ and $\gamma_1=s-(\alpha_x-1)$ ($s$, $\alpha_x$ the proton and target photon indices), and $E_{m br}\propto[(1+ ar z)\varepsilon_0]^{-1}$. The break width bounds the total smearing to $\sigma_s\le0.235$ dex (68% CL), no broader than redshift alone must make it, and the seed scale is the same across sources to within a factor $\lesssim$1.5, which mean-spectrum fits do not provide. Below-break neutrinos are predicted to come on average from higher redshifts than those above. The threshold also fixes the flavor and $
u/ ar
u$ composition, including the energy-dependent $ ar
u_e$ fraction and the Glashow-resonance discriminator of Winter et al., matching current flavor data. Inverted source by source, the relation gives each resolved IceCube source its target photon scale, from the keV coronae of NGC 1068 and PKS 1424+240 to the $\sim$20 eV jet of TXS 0506+056. That two-decade spread means they cannot supply the homogeneous break, which requires a separate, fainter population. KM3-230213A points to a warm-dust target, $\varepsilon_0\simeq0.02$ eV, unless cosmogenic.
item.dc:creator: Vernon Barger

item.title: Early Evolution of Strange Quark Stars Admixed with Fermionic Dark Matter
item.description: arXiv:2611.28054v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study strange quark stars admixed with fermionic dark matter (DM) in three quasistatic stages of their early evolution: the neutrino-trapped stage, the heated stage after deleptonization, and the cold stage. Quark matter is described by the MIT bag model at finite temperature with thermal gluons, a repulsive vector interaction, and, in the first stage, trapped neutrinos. The DM is modeled as a cold, asymmetric gas of fermions with masses $m_\chi = 0.3$, $1$, and $3$ GeV, with and without a repulsive self-interaction, and interacts with the quark matter only through gravity. Using the two-fluid Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equations, we compute the structure, the maximum masses, and the tidal deformability of the stars in each stage for DM mass fractions $F_D$ up to $5\%$, and we follow individual stars at fixed numbers of baryons and DM particles. The effect of DM is nearly the same in the three stages: for $m_\chi = 1$ GeV and $F_D = 5\%$, DM lowers the maximum mass by about $8\%$ and the tidal deformability of a $1.4\,M_\odot$ star by about $26\%$ in each stage, whereas the stage itself changes these quantities by only a few percent. Heavy DM forms a compact core; for $m_\chi = 3$ GeV without self-interaction, the mass limit of this core can set the maximum mass of the star. Light DM can form an extended halo, which does not increase the maximum mass for the fractions considered. For $m_\chi = 1$ GeV and $F_D = 5\%$, DM lowers the largest baryon mass of a newborn star by about $0.23\,M_\odot$, but this limit increases from the neutrino-trapped to the cold stage in all cases considered, so that DM does not cause a delayed collapse to a black hole. In our model, pulsars of about $2\,M_\odot$ require a stiff quark equation of state and restrict the DM fraction to a few percent unless the DM is light.
item.dc:creator: Rajasmita Sahoo, Mrutunjaya Bhuyan

item.title: Regge-eikonal description of high-energy proton-proton elastic scattering: a single-channel Gaussian benchmark confronted with TOTEM data at $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV
item.description: arXiv:2611.28140v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A single-Pomeron Regge Born amplitude with a Gaussian dependence on the momentum transfer is eikonalized in impact-parameter space, and the resulting single-channel, purely absorptive amplitude is evaluated in closed form. The total, elastic and inelastic cross sections and the forward slope are expressed through the entire exponential integral Ein(a) and a related series $I_1(a)$, and the closed forms are verified against direct numerical integration and against the weak-coupling Born limit. Two parameter choices are confronted with the TOTEM measurements at $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV. With the Donnachie-Landshoff trajectory and a normalization fixed at 7 TeV, the model gives $\sigma_{tot}=139.2$ mb against the measured $110.6\pm3.4$ mb and places the first diffractive zero at $|t|=0.244$ GeV$^2$ against the measured dip at 0.47 GeV$^2$. Calibration of the two parameters to the measured $\sigma_{tot}$ and $\sigma_{el}/\sigma_{tot}$ describes the differential cross section to within five per cent for $|t|\lesssim0.1$ GeV$^2$, but places the zero at 0.315 GeV$^2$ and overestimates the cross section at the measured dip by more than an order of magnitude. A single Gaussian opacity therefore cannot simultaneously accommodate the integrated cross sections and the position of the diffractive dip. Restoring the signature phase gives $\rho=0.098$, in agreement with the TOTEM and ATLAS measurements, and fills the zero without moving it; a two-component opacity reduces the excess at the dip from a factor of 15 to a factor of 2 without reproducing the dip-bump structure and the large-$|t|$ tail simultaneously; a two-channel Good-Walker eikonal on a Gaussian profile moves the minimum further away from the measured dip.
item.dc:creator: Ji Li

item.title: HEP-Ex-Bench: Evaluating Agentic Performance in High Energy Physics Experiment Data Analyses with Sealed Worlds
item.description: arXiv:2611.28194v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Agentic systems are increasingly being explored for automating experimental high-energy physics measurements, but the correctness of their results can today be reliably evaluated only via extensive expert review. To address this, we propose a method to perform detailed quantitative evaluations of agent-driven analyses through the use of blind analysis and injection tests, which are critical in a typical expert review. Agents develop a data analysis pipeline on a public dataset, while the evaluation is performed on programmatically generated sealed private datasets where signals are injected and simulation settings varied within realistic detector uncertainties. By requiring agents to provide a single workflow that is evaluated across these "sealed worlds", we are able to test the accuracy and robustness of the workflows. We demonstrate the approach on four tasks built from CMS open data and present it as a way to reliably benchmark scientific work in experimental high-energy physics. At the time of writing, the best-performing model, Gemini 4 Argon, reaches 60% of the score of the expert reference analyses on average, ahead of GPT 6 Astra at 38% and Claude Opus 5.5 at 31%. In individual sessions on one of the tasks, Gemini 4 Argon exceeds the reference. The benchmark is hosted at https://hep-ex-bench.github.io
item.dc:creator: Andrzej Nov\'ak, Yiyang Zhao, Dolores Garcia, Eric A. Moreno, Jeffrey Krupa, V\'ictor Bres\'o-Pla, Samuel Bright-Thonney, Lukas Heinrich, Michael Kagan, Philip Harris

item.title: A Transformer-based Method for Neutrino Event Generator Reweighting
item.description: arXiv:2611.28199v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The ability to test the effects of different neutrino event generators on simulation-based analyses is currently bottlenecked by the computational cost of propagating simulated events through expensive detector simulations. One way to circumvent this limitation is to reweight events produced with one generator to replicate the predictions of another. However, existing methods for doing this in neutrino physics tend to be limited to only a few observables at a time. We present a transformer-based architecture that can reweight between neutrino event generators based on nearly the entire particle stack, providing reweighted events that are valid over a greatly expanded phase space. We present results with events generated from multiple GENIE configurations and NuWro as examples, and we introduce an energy distance-based metric for evaluating the results in a multidimensional, unbinned manner. Our results show promising performance for realistic applications and provide a method for comparing the performance of different reweighting techniques.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Cudd, Roger G. Huang, Benjamin Nachman, Vinicius Mikuni, Callum Wilkinson

item.title: An all-orders proof of gradient flow for multiscalar $\phi^4$ theory in four dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.28206v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that the renormalisation group flow of multiscalar $\phi^4$ theory in four dimensions is a gradient flow to all orders in perturbation theory. The proof uses the Weyl consistency conditions of Osborn and Jack, and it assumes two properties of perturbation theory: that the generating functional with local couplings is finite (also assumed by Osborn and Jack), and that the known expansion of massive Feynman integrals at large momenta holds with a bound on its remainder at each momentum. The consistency conditions give a gradient formula in which the tensor that multiplies the beta function is allowed to have an antisymmetric part, determined by coefficients of the Weyl anomaly. We derive a Ward identity for the two-point function of the marginal operators at constant couplings away from fixed points, with sources for the currents of field rotations and for the mass operator. It re-expresses one of the anti-symmetric contributions in terms of two-point functions and the first moment of the three-point function. We show that, after this rewrite, each of the resulting terms is equivalent to a symmetric contribution to the metric and a contribution to the potential, and we give both explicitly. The metric is positive definite to all orders in perturbation theory. The proof implies in particular the four relations among five- and six-loop coefficients of the field rotation, which Pannell and Stergiou derived as the conditions for a gradient flow at six loops. We check by explicit computation that these relations indeed hold. A companion paper treats $d=4-\varepsilon$ and other critical dimensions with a Ward identity on the sphere.
item.dc:creator: Marten Reehorst

item.title: Bring Your Own Instanton: Monopole Catalysis from Sourced SU(2) Instantons
item.description: arXiv:2611.28208v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that Rubakov-Callan catalysis of proton decay in the field of a 't Hooft-Polyakov monopole proceeds through "sourced SU(2) instantons", which are novel topological gauge configurations sourced by fermions and carrying unit instanton number. Unlike vacuum BPST instantons, these sourced instantons do not give rise to exponentially suppressed rates. We relate the winding number to the number of fermionic zero modes, suggesting an underlying index theorem for sourced instantons. We also calculate the closed-form expression for the leading-order correlator for fermion insertions both outside and inside the monopole core. Our results indicate that Rubakov-Callan catalysis is an IR effect where the scattering fermions do not reach the monopole core.
item.dc:creator: Csaba Cs\'aki, Larissa Kiriliuk, Zhihan Liu, Rotem Ovadia

item.title: Exploring the phase diagram of dense and hot matter with HBT interferometry
item.description: arXiv:2611.28513v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the HBT radii of pions produced in Au+Au collisions at selected energies from the STAR-BES program, using an event-by-event hybrid model that combines AMPT initial conditions, 3+1D viscous hydrodynamic evolution with a QCD equation of state at finite baryon chemical potential, and hadronic transport with SMASH. The goal is to explore the source's space-time structure and its possible connection to the structure of the QCD phase diagram. The hybrid chain was first validated by comparing identified-particle spectra and anisotropic flow, yielding a globally consistent description of the experimental data, with more evident discrepancies at the lowest energies.
item.dc:creator: Vin\'icius S. Fran\c{c}\~ao, Fr\'ed\'erique Grassi

item.title: Measuring the Neutrino Mass with $^{241}$Pu
item.description: arXiv:2611.29122v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Tritium has long been the isotope of choice for measurements of the absolute neutrino mass. Its low nuclear mass leads to substantial recoil energy, limiting measurements with both molecular tritium ($T_2$) and atomic tritium bound to a substrate. With a beta-decay endpoint energy and half-life similar to those of tritium, but a much larger nuclear mass, $^{241}$Pu may offer an interesting alternative. Its principal challenge is background from the beta decay of $^{237}$U. We discuss strategies for suppressing this background and compare the projected neutrino-mass sensitivities of $^{241}$Pu and tritium as a function of the background suppression.
item.dc:creator: Mustafa Anaam (Radboud University), Nicolo de Groot (Radboud University), Inge van Rens (Radboud University)

item.title: Thermodynamics of QCD+QED from the lattice
item.description: arXiv:2611.29423v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: QED corrections to observables in QCD are by now well-understood at zero temperature, where QED effects are perturbative and required for precision physics observables, such as the neutron-proton mass difference or the muon anomalous magnetic moment, among many others. However, there are indications in the literature that at finite temperature the introduction of QED can lead to non-perturbative effects, affecting the structure of the phase diagram, since the combined theory is exactly center-symmetric. In this proceedings article, we analyze the structure of the combined theory and the different strategies to simulate it on the lattice, as well as presenting novel results of lattice QCD+QED simulations at finite temperature, focusing on understanding the role of the electromagnetic coupling in the thermodynamics of this system. We also discuss new features that arise in the combined theory and the challenges that these simulations entail, which require the development of new algorithms in order to understand the phase diagram of QCD+QED from first principles.
item.dc:creator: G. Endr\H{o}di, E. Garnacho-Velasco, G. Mark\'{o}, L. Peth\H{o}

item.title: Quadratic-in-spin scattering of compact bodies at fourth post-Minkowskian order
item.description: arXiv:2611.29670v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present the fourth-post-Minkowskian scattering angle of aligned spinning compact bodies through quadratic spin at arbitrary velocity and mass ratio. We include spin-induced quadrupoles and radiation reaction, supplemented by curvature-squared spin-tidal terms. Three-loop worldline integrals yield closed forms in polylogarithms and elliptic integrals. Infrared poles cancel exactly, fixing the tail logarithm. We obtain a new post-Newtonian coefficient and third-order angular-momentum loss for general quadrupoles. The new input shifts resummed predictions for black-hole scattering.
item.dc:creator: Taushif Ahmed, Syed Mehedi Hasan

item.title: Hadron spectroscopy of QC2D at finite density
item.description: arXiv:2611.29900v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the chemical-potential dependence of hadron masses in two-color QCD (QC$_2$D) at low temperature using lattice Monte Carlo simulations.
