We calculate all possible meson and diquark correlation functions, including disconnected diagrams, on a $32^4$ lattice at $T\approx40\,\mathrm{MeV}$. In the hadronic phase, we obtain a meson mass hierarchy similar to that of three-color QCD. After the superfluid transition, the ordering changes: the $\sigma$ and $a_1$ channels become lighter, while the pion mass increases with density. We also examine the diquark source dependence of the Nambu--Goldstone mode of $U(1)_B$ symmetry breaking and find an almost vanishing mass in the superfluid phase after extrapolation to zero source. Finally, we compare correlation functions for chiral partners and discuss indications of partial chiral-symmetry restoration. This contribution is based on our recent study of hadron spectra in dense QC$_2$D~\cite{Iida:2026dmw}.
item.dc:creator: Kei Iida, Etsuko Itou, Kotaro Murakami, and Daiki Suenaga

item.title: Ionization of gravitational atoms by a companion-sourced Yukawa potential
item.description: arXiv:2611.29939v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Superradiant instabilities around rotating black holes can produce clouds of ultralight bosons bound by the black hole's gravitational field. A binary companion can ionize these clouds by driving transitions into continuum states in the black hole's 1/r gravitational potential, extracting energy and angular momentum from the orbit. We investigate how a companion-sourced Yukawa interaction modifies this process. At weak coupling, the interference term between the gravitational and Yukawa transition amplitudes provides the leading correction to the ionization power. For the orbital frequencies here, an attractive interaction enhances continuum ionization and accelerates the inspiral, whereas a repulsive interaction has the opposite effect. At larger coupling, the pure Yukawa contribution to the ionization power becomes increasingly important and can compete with the gravitational contribution, particularly for lighter mediators. Comparing continuum ionization with off-resonant bound-state mixing, we find that continuum ionization can halt superradiant growth at a substantially smaller Yukawa coupling. At their respective critical couplings, the Yukawa interaction provides the dominant contribution to cloud depletion in both channels. Finally, we calculate the phase correction to gravitational waves due to continuum ionization and characterize how the chirp-rate response varies with frequency near the thresholds at which successive orbital harmonics open continuum-ionization channels.
item.dc:creator: Yi Wang, Jiayi Yao

item.title: Dark matter mass fraction in axion stars
item.description: arXiv:2611.30321v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: QCD axion dark matter is fragmented into small mass miniclusters of high density. With the natural parameters of miniclusters, the time for Bose-Einstein condensation is less than the age of the Universe, which leads to the formation of Bose stars inside these structures. Recently, the problem of the subsequent growth of Bose stars was solved analytically (Dmitriev et al, Phys. Rev. Lett. 132, 091001 (2024)). We use this solution to determine present day mass fraction of dark matter in Bose stars and their mass function.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Dmitriev, A.S., Levkov, D.G., Panin, A.G. et al. Dark Matter Mass Fraction in Axion Stars. Jetp Lett. (2026)
item.dc:creator: A. S. Dmitriev, D. G. Levkov, A. G. Panin, I. I. Tkachev

item.title: Revealing Nuclear Shape through Identified-Hadron Flow Decorrelations
item.description: arXiv:2611.30429v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Relativistic nuclear collisions encode nuclear shape in collective flow, yet the potential of identified hadrons to disentangle deformation modes remains largely unexplored. Using event-by-event viscous hydrodynamics coupled to hadronic transport, we investigate momentum-dependent elliptic-flow decorrelations of pions, kaons, and protons in central $^{238}$U+$^{238}$U collisions at 193 GeV and $^{20}$Ne+$^{20}$Ne collisions at 5.36 TeV. The identified species exhibit distinct momentum- and deformation-dependent responses, with nuclear-shape information persisting in their relative correlations even when individual deformation effects are weak. We introduce crossing coordinates $(P_{\rm cross},R_{\rm cross})$, defined by the intersection of pion-kaon and pion-proton flow-factorization ratios. Variations of quadrupole deformation and triaxiality generate distinct trajectories in the crossing plane, offering complementary constraints on both nuclear-shape parameters. The corresponding behavior persists in higher-moment correlations, while an energy comparison in Ne+Ne reveals the influence of collision dynamics. Our findings establish identified-particle flow decorrelations as a complementary approach to probing and constraining intrinsic nuclear geometry.
item.dc:creator: Hadi Mehrabpour, Abhisek Saha, Li Yan

item.title: Conservative tidal effects to third post-Minkowskian order in scalar-tensor theories
item.description: arXiv:2611.30762v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Using worldline effective field theory, we compute the conservative finite-size contributions to the impulse and scattering angle of nonspinning compact binaries in massless scalar-tensor theories with a scalar-Gauss-Bonnet coupling through third post-Minkowskian (3PM) order. We retain the full velocity dependence at linear order in the tidal response coefficients. The calculation covers the scalar dipole and quadrupole and the electric, magnetic, and mixed quadrupoles and octupoles. Among them, the scalar dipole enters the dynamics already at third post-Newtonian (3PN) order, two orders before the gravitational quadrupole. At 3PM, the tidal correction to the angle also depends on the first scalar derivatives of the responses and contains terms linear in the Gauss-Bonnet coupling. The results reproduce the general-relativistic tidal angle and the post-Newtonian tidal dynamics through 5PN, and a test-body calculation confirms their leading order in the mass ratio, including the Gauss-Bonnet terms for a companion with vanishing sensitivity.
item.dc:creator: Zhengwen Liu, Hongbin Wang

item.title: Unbinned Likelihoods for Probability Densities with Poles
item.description: arXiv:2611.30877v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Unbinned likelihood fits to detector-level data become prohibitively expensive when narrow resonances interfere with a nonresonant amplitude. The convolution of the truth-level probability density with the detector resolution must then resolve the resonances, whose widths are much smaller than the resolution. We propose a simple approach that subtracts one simple-pole term per resonance from the probability density. This term captures the resonant contribution in closed form, and the smooth remainder is convolved numerically on a grid whose spacing is set by the resolution alone. The approach applies to multidimensional densities and to densities known only on the real axis. Using two benchmark problems, we quantify the accuracy, computational cost, and statistical impact of the approach. We emphasise that the subtraction is a general approach to the computational problems of unbinned likelihoods in the presence of poles in their probability density and that it is applicable to a wide variety of problems in experimental particle physics.
item.dc:creator: M\'eril Reboud, Danny van Dyk, Matteo Verzeletti

item.title: Finite Temperature Isoscalar Instabilities and Moat Regimes in Relativistic Nuclear Matter
item.description: arXiv:2611.31040v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the finite-temperature isoscalar collective response of symmetric nuclear matter in three relativistic mean-field descriptions: the linear Walecka model, its nonlinear extension, and the quark-meson coupling (QMC) model. The Walecka models are formulated in terms of nucle- onic degrees of freedom, whereas QMC incorporates quark degrees of freedom confined inside the nucleon. These models differ in their treatment of scalar interactions at finite density, affecting instability boundaries. Focusing on the coupled scalar-vector channel, we track how the boundaries of homogeneous instabilities evolve with temperature. In all three models, we find a nonmonotonic momentum dependence of the static response, characterized by a minimum at finite momentum, a moat regime that selects a preferred length scale for density fluctuations. Our results show that this moat structure is robust against thermal effects across these relativistic nuclear matter models, providing motivation for future studies of inhomogeneous phases in hot and dense astrophysical matter.
item.dc:creator: Randall H. V. Pradinett, Theo F. Motta, Gast\~ao Krein

item.title: Gradient formula from the sphere for perturbative RG flows near critical dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.31050v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the gradient property of perturbative renormalisation group flows in $d=d_c-\varepsilon$, with a potential and a metric regular at $\varepsilon=0$ up to logarithms of gauge couplings. We state properties of the renormalised functional with local couplings on the sphere $S^d$: finiteness, a local Weyl anomaly, the Ward identity of a conformal Killing vector, rotation properties and statements on the free theory. From them we derive a Ward identity without anomaly for a combination of the functional and its anomaly. Its first variation is a gradient formula whose symmetric metric contains the two-point function on the sphere and whose potential at fixed points is, in an extended form of the properties, proportional to the sphere free energy $\tilde F$ up to a constant. Sources of relevant operators enter through their Weyl variation, and in a scheme which we construct the gradient formula persists, with a nondegenerate metric if a matrix of the free theory is invertible. For multiscalar $\phi^4$ theory and for scalars and Dirac fermions with Yukawa and quartic couplings in $d=4-\varepsilon$, for sextic scalars in $d=3-\varepsilon$ and for cubic scalars in $d=6-\varepsilon$, we derive all these properties from a finiteness hypothesis. The gradient formula then holds to all orders for the beta function defined on the sphere. For interacting gauge theories the properties remain assumptions.
item.dc:creator: Marten Reehorst

item.title: Electromagnetic Memory as a Collider Observable
item.description: arXiv:2611.31107v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Electromagnetic memory and charge correlators are measured by different detectors, sensitive to soft radiation and to hard charged tracks. We show that the Ward identity of large gauge symmetry relates these quantities as inclusive observables. For lepton pairs produced by an electromagnetic current, we compute all massless multipoint memory correlators and the massive two-point function, whose coincident limit gives the soft photon number. The correlators admit a celestial free-boson representation and remain finite at first radiative order, where recoil generates back-to-back Sudakov logarithms.
item.dc:creator: Felipe Diaz, Hern\'an A. Gonz\'alez, Oriana Labrin, Jakob Salzer

item.title: The Sensitivity of Gamma-Ray Searches for Dark Matter Annihilation in Milky Way Dwarf Galaxies: the LSST Era and Beyond
item.description: arXiv:2611.31130v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We forecast the sensitivity of gamma-ray searches to dark matter annihilation in Milky Way satellite dwarf galaxies using BabyBison, a Monte Carlo pipeline combining cosmological satellite simulations and observational selection functions with a joint likelihood analysis of gamma-ray data. Although LSST is expected to substantially expand the catalog of known satellite galaxies, we find that these discoveries are likely to produce only modest improvements in the resulting dark matter annihilation constraints, typically below 20\%. Much more substantial gains are possible, however, in relatively rare realizations that contain yet-to-be-discovered satellites with large $J$-factors. These results reinforce the fact that indirect detection analyses using the population of dwarf galaxies are typically driven in large part by a small number of high-$J$-factor systems rather than by the total satellite count. We present projections for the sensitivity of Fermi-LAT and the proposed Advanced Particle-astrophysics Telescope (APT) to dark matter annihilation, finding that a complete census of the Milky Way dwarf sample could enable such instruments to probe dark matter with masses up to the TeV scale. We also investigate the dark matter discovery potential of these instruments and project their ability to measure the properties of an annihilating dark matter particle.
item.dc:creator: Ilumi Chavez, Aditya Ghosh, Chris Kelso, Dan Hooper, Alex Drlica-Wagner, Ethan O. Nadler

item.title: Massive de Sitter correlators at one loop
item.description: arXiv:2611.31214v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Fermions and massive fields charged under an unbroken symmetry couple to the inflaton only in pairs, so their signals in primordial correlators begin at one loop. Templates for these signals are mostly late-time estimates. Starting from a representation of massive de Sitter correlators as finite Mellin-Barnes integrals, we compute the exact squeezed coefficients of these signals and their corrections away from the squeezed limit. The leading coefficient factorizes into a hard part and a soft vertex. Late-time estimates treat the hard part exactly but approximate the soft vertex by its late-time limit, whereas we compute both exactly. Without a chemical potential, the exact coefficient differs from the late-time one by a universal factor that depends only on the masses in the loop and the coupling at the soft vertex. For the heavy Standard Model loops, the exact signals are ten to thirty times larger than their late-time estimates. With a chemical potential, the ratio depends on the model, and at our benchmarks it reaches a factor of thirty for helical vectors and about a hundred for the fermion triangle, where we agree with recent exact results. Away from the squeezed limit the leading term soon fails, mainly through a drift in the phase of the oscillation, which we derive for scalar and fermion loops.
item.dc:creator: Amara McCune

item.title: Precise predictions for double-Higgs production via vector-boson fusion
item.description: arXiv:2005.13341v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Theoretical predictions with next-to-next-to-leading order (NNLO) QCD accuracy combined with the next-to-leading order (NLO) electroweak (EW) corrections are presented for differential observables of the double-Higgs production process via vector-boson fusion. While the QCD corrections were previously known, the EW ones are computed here for the first time. The numerical results are obtained for a realistic experimental set-up at the LHC and are presented in the form of fiducial cross sections and differential distributions. Within this setup we find that the VBF approximation employed in the NNLO QCD correction is accurate at the sub-percent level. We find that the NLO EW corrections within the fiducial volume are $-4.8\%$, making them of almost the same order as the NLO QCD corrections. In some kinematic regions they can grow as large as $-30\%$ making them the dominant radiative corrections. When the EW corrections are combined with the NNLO QCD corrections we find a total correction of $-14.8\%$. The results presented here thus comprise the state-of-the-art theoretical predicition for the double-Higgs production via vector-boson fusion, which will be of value to the high-luminosity programme at the LHC.
item.dc:creator: Fr\'ed\'eric A. Dreyer, Alexander Karlberg, Jean-Nicolas Lang, Mathieu Pellen

item.title: Soft photon corrections in $B \to K^{(\ast)} \ell^+ \ell^-$ and $\Lambda_b \to \Lambda^{(\ast)} \ell^+ \ell^-$ decays
item.description: arXiv:2307.07578v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We calculate QED corrections to the semileptonic decays $H_1\to H_2\ell^+\ell^-$ where $\ell=e, \mu$ and $H_{1,2}$ are hadrons. The soft and/or collinear divergences are regulated in a gauge-invariant manner and demonstrably cancel, leaving behind a finite residue that depends on the (infrared) momentum cutoff below which a photon is considered to be indistinguishable. On resumming, the said sensitivity reduces drastically, {\em i.e.}, for the NLL result as compared to the NLO one. The overall correction is negative and its magnitude is larger for a lighter lepton. The corrections are presented for $B\to K^{(*)}$ and, for the first time, for $\Lambda_b\to\Lambda^{(*)}$ decays. Given that QED final-state radiation is routinely incorporated in experimental Monte Carlo simulations, for example through PHOTOS, our results provide an important theoretical framework for assessing the accuracy and limitations of these simulations and their impact on LFU observables such as $R_{K^{(*)}}$.
item.dc:creator: Debajyoti Choudhury, Diganta Das, Jaydeb Das

item.title: The Chiral Lagrangian of CP-Violating Axion-Like Particles
item.description: arXiv:2311.12158v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We discuss the construction of the most general CP-violating chiral Lagrangian for an axion-like particle (ALP). Starting with an effective Lagrangian containing light quarks and gluons, we provide its matching onto a chiral effective Lagrangian at $\mathcal{O}(p^2)$ described in terms of mesons and baryons, identifying the correspondence between the Jarlskog invariants of the two theories. After deriving the ALP interactions with mesons and baryons, we analyse a few relevant phenomenological implications such as the permanent electric dipole moments of nucleons and the CP-violating ALP and kaon decays.This work provides the necessary tools for further phenomenological analyses connecting low-energy observables with the couplings of the underlying ultraviolet complete theory.
item.dc:creator: Luca Di Luzio, Gabriele Levati, Paride Paradisi

item.title: Local-equilibrium theory of neutrino oscillations
item.description: arXiv:2506.03271v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Miscidynamics describes coarse-grained neutrino transport under the assumption that flavor mixing is in local equilibrium. Here we introduce the concept of turbulent flavor-wave viscosity and develop techniques for including it in miscidynamics. This extension of the theory is necessary when neutrinos develop weak flavor instabilities as a result of astrophysical driving. The flavor-wave dispersion relation is obtained using a new and more general form of linear analysis, which does not require small flavor coherence. Flavor-wave transport is then approximated using wave kinetics and geometric optics. We hypothesize that the dynamical emergence of local oscillation invariants restricts the extent of flavor thermalization. In this view, flavor evolution is sculpted by both entropy-increasing and order-promoting factors.
item.dc:creator: Lucas Johns, Anson Kost

item.title: Integrated subtraction terms and finite remainders for arbitrary processes with massless partons at colliders in the nested soft-collinear subtraction scheme
item.description: arXiv:2509.08594v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present integrated subtraction terms and finite remainders for arbitrary processes with massless partons at hadron and lepton colliders in the context of the nested soft-collinear subtraction scheme. These results provide the very last ingredients needed to make this scheme a fully local, analytic and process-independent framework for treating infrared singularities at next-to-next-to-leading order in perturbative QCD. The explicit infrared finiteness of all required contributions, as well as their process-independence, puts these results on par with subtraction schemes developed for next-to-leading order computations and opens up a clear path towards the automation of next-to-next-to-leading order computations in QCD.
item.dc:creator: Federica Devoto, Kirill Melnikov, Raoul R\"ontsch, Chiara Signorile-Signorile, Davide Maria Tagliabue, Matteo Tresoldi

item.title: A Coupled Source Description of Pseudorapidity Distributions from RHIC to LHC: Emergent $1/\mu_B$ Scaling and Limiting Fragmentation
item.description: arXiv:2512.01360v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: One of the most remarkable observations in heavy-ion collisions is the systematic regularity exhibited by pseudorapidity distributions of charged particles across collision energies. While single-source models fail at higher energies and independent multi-source approaches do not reproduce the central dip observed at LHC energies, a unified description across the full RHIC-LHC energy range remains elusive. These distributions from Au+Au collisions at RHIC ($\sqrt{s_{NN}}$ = 19.6--200 GeV) and Pb+Pb collisions at LHC ($\sqrt{s_{NN}}$ = 2.76--5.36 TeV) are analyzed using a novel parametrization based on coupled Gaussian sources where the interaction strength is quantified by parameter $\lambda$. This coupled two-source model captures the interaction between forward and backward sources through the medium formed in the collision. Remarkably, $\lambda$ exhibits empirical scaling behavior resembling $1/\mu_B$, suggesting sensitivity to baryon stopping and the strongly-interacting medium. All fitting parameters follow systematic energy trends, with the peak-to-peak distance and chemical freeze-out temperature exhibiting identical exponential saturation patterns, indicating that geometric expansion and thermal evolution share a common underlying dynamics governed by QCD phase structure. Furthermore, the approach naturally preserves limiting fragmentation behavior across all energies, in contrast to independent source models that suggest its violation at LHC energies. Although the theoretical basis requires further investigation, these empirical correlations successfully unify charged particle production across nearly two orders of magnitude in collision energy, revealing fundamental connections to underlying collision dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Neeraj, Md. Kaosar Ali Mondal, Amal Sarkar

item.title: Event-by-Event Multiplicity Cumulants as Probes of Partonic Energy Loss and Phase Structure in Au+Au Collisions within a Modified HIJING Model
item.description: arXiv:2603.09732v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Event-by-event fluctuations of charged hadron multiplicity, net-proton, and net-electric charge are investigated in central Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} =$ 20-200 GeV using a modified HIJING Monte Carlo generator. The model incorporates QCD-inspired partonic energy-loss formalisms in hot (quark--gluon plasma) and cold media, reducing reliance on the default HIJING energy-loss parameter. At energies above 100 GeV/nucleon, multiplicity and net-charge fluctuations show sensitivity to the assumed medium properties, while net-proton results provide an additional comparison with available STAR measurements. By introducing a probabilistic distribution for a first-order phase transition, we find within the present modified-HIJING framework that multiplicity cumulant ratios ($\sigma^2/M$ and $S\sigma$) show a pronounced non-linear response to the adopted phase-allocation ansatz near the selected binodal energy, whereas net-charge and net-proton fluctuations remain relatively insensitive. Furthermore, expanding the kinematic acceptance enhances the sensitivity of multiplicity fluctuations to the selected transition region in the present phenomenological ansatz.
item.dc:creator: Y. A. Rusak, L. F. Babichev

item.title: Axionlike Particles and Lepton Flavor Violation in Muonic Atoms
item.description: arXiv:2604.07481v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We explore the potential of the Mu2e experiment to probe the lepton-flavor-violating process $\mu^- e^- \to e^- e^-$ in a muonic atom within a simplified axion-like particle (ALP) framework featuring flavor-violating $e$-$\mu$ couplings and a flavor-diagonal pseudoscalar coupling to electrons, which also allows for possible invisible ALP decays into a dark sector. We compute the ALP-mediated contribution to the transition rate and show that, at fixed couplings, the branching ratio increases for lighter mediators and scales as $(Z-1)^3$, favoring heavier nuclei. We compare the model against constraints from $\mu\to e\gamma$, $\mu\to 3e$, $\mu\to e\gamma\gamma$, $\mu\to e+\mathrm{inv}$, and muonium-antimuonium conversion, as well as from the anomalous magnetic moments of the electron and muon. Additional astrophysical and beam-dump limits on the electron coupling are also discussed. A key result is that $\Delta a_e$ provides one of the most stringent probes of the parameter space and, in the global scan, excludes the largest fraction of sampled points. After applying the laboratory constraints used in the scan, the viable branching ratio for $\mu^- e^- \to e^- e^-$ in aluminum drops to at most $\mathcal{O}(10^{-20})$, while the resonant region $2m_e<m_a<m_\mu-m_e$ is much more heavily suppressed. The highest achievable values are closely tied to $\mathcal{B}(\mu\to 3e)$ near its current limit, indicating that the upcoming Mu3e experiment will explore the most promising region relevant for this muonic-atom signal. Our analysis shows that, although a light ALP can parametrically enhance $\mu^- e^- \to e^- e^-$ at fixed couplings, existing bounds -- especially $\Delta a_e$, $\mu\to 3e$, $\mu\to e\gamma$, and muonium oscillations -- severely limit the observable rate.
item.dc:creator: Girish Kumar, Alexey A. Petrov

item.title: A High-Precision Statistical Analysis of the SN1987A Neutrino Temporal Distribution
item.description: arXiv:2605.06401v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The interpretation of the SN1987A neutrino data remains limited by significant absolute timing uncertainties across independent detectors and a long-standing tension in the angular distributions. This work presents a high-precision statistical framework that resolves these issues by formalizing the mathematical distinction between intrinsic and relative timing offsets (ITOs and RTOs). By performing a simultaneous $\chi^2$-alignment of the Kamiokande-II and Baksan data with the IMB clock, we systematically incorporate non-Gaussian statistical correlations, reducing the temporal uncertainty by two orders of magnitude to the sub-second level. The $\chi^2$-analysis shows that Baksan's absolute timestamps require an advancement of $30.4\,\rm s$, while those of Kamiokande-II require a delay of about $6.4\,\rm s$. Establishing this unified, high-precision timeline is critical to test the physical nature of the first Kamiokande-II event (K1), specifically whether its distinct angular features signal the onset of the prompt neutronization burst. Previous literature often assumes that K1 originated from inverse beta decay (IBD) on qualitative grounds. By contrast, our multidimensional likelihood analysis incorporates energy, direction, and MSW flavor-conversion effects to provide the first quantitative constraint on its origin. We find a likelihood ratio of 3-6 in favor of an accretion-phase $\bar{\nu}_e$ origin over a neutronization-burst origin, thereby turning a traditional assumption into a statistically bounded physical inference. This framework provides the most stringent constraints to date on the chronology of SN1987A and establishes a precise methodology for future multimessenger observations of Galactic supernovae.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: The European Physical Journal C, Volume 86, article number 1332 (2026)
item.dc:creator: Riccardo Maria Bozza, Vigilante di Risi, Veronica Oliviero, Giulia Ricciardi, Francesco Vissani

item.title: Forward hadron production in pp collisions at LHC energies from an event generator based on the color glass condensate framework
item.description: arXiv:2605.15494v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate inclusive forward single-hadron production in high-energy proton--proton collisions using a CGC-inspired Monte Carlo event generator, MC-CGC. We carried out a systematic study of the sensitivity of the running-coupling Balitsky-Kovchegov (rcBK) evolution equation to its initial conditions by comparing three parameterizations: the McLerran-Venugopalan (MV) model and its two HERA DIS-constrained variants, MV$^\gamma$ and MV$^e$. Our results indicate that the current LHCb data favor the MV$^\gamma$ and MV$^e$ models, while the differences from the original MV model become more pronounced at higher transverse momentum and at mid-rapidity. As a complementary analysis, we also compared the dilute-dense (DHJ factorization) and dense-dense ($k_T$ factorization) frameworks. We found that the $k_T$ factorization framework provides a better description of the particle production spectra at mid-rapidity than the DHJ framework, where both the projectile and target are in the dense regime at LHC energies. Predictions for the FoCal measurements at ALICE, including the production of identified neutral mesons and jets, are also presented.
item.dc:creator: Hirotsugu Fujii, Tetsufumi Hirano, Kazunori Itakura, Yasushi Nara, Shujun Zhao

item.title: Modern Determination of Pion and Kaon Fragmentation Functions from SIA and High-Precision COMPASS SIDIS Multiplicities
item.description: arXiv:2606.16754v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present two separate determinations of charged-pion and charged-kaon fragmentation functions (FFs), denoted HAPS-PiFF1.0 and HAPS-KaFF1.0, at next-to-leading order (NLO) and within a next-to-next-to-leading-order (NNLO) perturbative QCD setup. The analysis combines single-inclusive electron-positron annihilation (SIA) data with charge-separated semi-inclusive deep-inelastic-scattering (SIDIS) multiplicities from HERMES and COMPASS. A central goal of this work is to incorporate the modern COMPASS SIDIS input, namely the COMPASS 2025 proton-target multiplicities and the COMPASS 2026 revised isoscalar-target multiplicities, into a common charged-pion and charged-kaon FF analysis and to assess their role in the resulting flavor separation. The revised isoscalar data supersede the earlier COMPASS measurements used in previous global fits. The charge-separated pion multiplicities provide important constraints on favored and unfavored light-quark fragmentation, while the kaon measurements enhance the sensitivity to light-quark, unfavored, and strange-to-kaon fragmentation channels. In both analyses, the gluon FF remains indirectly constrained in the present SIA+SIDIS framework and should be interpreted with appropriate caution. The extractions are carried out using the publicly available MontBlanc framework, and the resulting HAPS-PiFF1.0 and HAPS-KaFF1.0 replica sets are provided in the standard LHAPDF format.
item.dc:creator: HAPS Collaboration, Maryam Soleymaninia, Hamzeh Khanpour, Hubert Spiesberger, Majid Azizi, Michael Klasen, Hadi Hashamipour

item.title: Chirality Observables in Vector-Like Lepton Doublet Pair Production with Polarized Beams at a 3 TeV Lepton Collider
item.description: arXiv:2606.28717v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study how pair production of a mass-degenerate weak-isodoublet vector-like lepton (VLL) depends on longitudinal beam polarization at the 3~TeV Compact Linear Collider (CLIC), for VLL masses of 1.1--1.4~TeV and mixing in the tau sector. The charged pair $e^+e^-\to\tau'\bar\tau'$ proceeds through photon and $Z$ exchange, the neutral pair $e^+e^-\to\nu'\bar\nu'$ through $Z$ exchange alone. For the baseline electron polarization $P_{e^-}=-0.8$, the tree-level rates at $\mvll=1.2$~TeV are 15.77~fb (charged) and 4.75~fb (neutral). For an optional positron polarization $P_{e^+}=+0.3$, the left--right configuration $(-0.8,+0.3)$ raises the two rates by factors of 1.95 and 1.38 relative to unpolarized beams. The charged--neutral rate contrast reaches $D_\sigma=0.546$ there, compared with $0.08$ for the opposite configuration, and the observed left--right asymmetries are 0.57 (charged) and 0.12 (neutral). These normalized quantities are independent of the VLL mass at Born level because both channels share the same phase-space factor. Unpolarized rates at a 3~TeV muon collider coincide with the unpolarized CLIC rates to within 0.2\%, as expected from lepton universality. A counting estimate gives a Gaussian separation of the two asymmetries of $Z_A\simeq9$ for a visible fraction of $10^{-1}$ and $Z_A\simeq2.7$--$2.9$ for $10^{-2}$ at $1~{\rm ab}^{-1}$. All results are tree-level, fixed-energy, production-level quantities; initial-state radiation, beamstrahlung, detector effects and backgrounds are not included, and no exclusion or discovery reach is claimed.
item.dc:creator: Haroon Sagheer, Ijaz Ahmed, Jamil Muhammad

item.title: 70 years of Double-Logarithmic Approximation
item.description: arXiv:2607.00771v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Existence of Double-Logarithmic (DL) contributions to scattering amplitudes in QED was discovered by V.V. Sudakov in 1956 and total summation of DL contributions to electron-photon scattering resulted in appearance of famous Sudakov exponentials. Then, thanks to contributions of V.G. Gorshkov, V.N. Gribov, G.V. Frolov and L.N. Lipatov, the pattern of calculations in Double- Logarithmic Approximation (DLA) was constructed. Since then, DLA has become one of basic ways of describing various high-energy processes in the framework of QED, QCD and theory of EW interactions. In the present paper, we remind the history of DLA and present a brief overview of application of DLA to various objects like form factors, scattering amplitudes, DIS structure functions.
item.dc:creator: B. I. Ermolaev

item.title: Possibility of the antibottom-strange molecular pentaquarks near $ B\Sigma$ and $ B^*\Sigma$ thresholds
item.description: arXiv:2607.04679v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The molecular states in coupled channel system of $B_s^0N- B\Lambda- B^*\Lambda- B\Sigma- B^*\Sigma$ are investigated within one-boson-exchange model that includes $S$-$D$ wave mixing and a tunable short-range $\delta(r)$ term. Bound, resonant, and virtual states are searched by analytically continuing the $S$ matrix in the complex energy plane. In the single-channel analysis, the $ B\Sigma$ and $ B^*\Sigma$ systems with $J^P=1/2^-$ and $3/2^-$ are found to be attractive and form three bound states with reasonable cutoff region, corresponding to $1/2^-( B\Sigma)$, $1/2^-( B^*\Sigma)$, and $3/2^-( B^*\Sigma)$ . When coupled-channel dynamics is included, these states evolve into near-threshold poles that produce enhancements in the $B_s^0N$, $ B\Lambda$, and $ B^*\Lambda$ invariant mass spectra. The pole below the $ B^*\Sigma$ threshold in the $J^P=1/2^-$ system depends strongly on the treatment of the short-range $\delta(r)$ term and becomes a virtual state when this contribution is removed, while the other two resonant poles and their line shapes are only moderately affected. The influences of $B^{(*)}\Sigma^*$ channels on these states are also investigated. For representative parameter region, the predicted masses of these states lie in the $6.44-6.70$ GeV region and have widths of a few to several MeV. The pole coupling and partial-width analyses indicate that the invariant mass spectrum of the $B_s^0N$ and $ B^{(*)}\Lambda$ channels are the best place to hunt the predicted states. These results support the existence of near-threshold molecular pentaquark $P_{ \bar b s}$ and provide useful guidance in future experimental searches.
item.dc:creator: Jian-Kang Zhao, Nijiati Yalikun

item.title: Formation and scaling of $\mathbb{Z}_N$ strings for global $\mathrm{SU}(N)/\mathbb{Z}_N$ symmetry
item.description: arXiv:2607.21701v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We numerically investigate networks of global $\mathbb{Z}_N$ strings with multi-string junctions in a scalar field model whose vacuum manifold is $\mathrm{PSU}(N)=\mathrm{SU}(N)/\mathbb{Z}_N$. The construction of the model is motivated by the Higgs vacua of mass-deformed $\mathcal{N}=4$ supersymmetric Yang--Mills theory, commonly known as $\mathcal{N}=1^*$ theory, and provides a tractable effective description of string networks with baryon-vertex-like junctions. We perform classical lattice simulations of the formation and evolution of these networks in a radiation-dominated universe. For $N=2,3,$ and $4$, the time histories suggest that the total winding-length density approaches approximate scaling over the simulated interval, with no evidence for frustration. For $N=5$ and $8$, we report densities at selected times. For the parameters studied, the density normalization grows approximately in proportion to $N^2-1$, while non-minimal-charge components remain subdominant.
item.dc:creator: Masaki Yamada

item.title: Three-body forces in the quark model
item.description: arXiv:2608.18949v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We review the connection between constituent-quark Hamiltonians and QCD and investigate the long-standing difficulty of describing meson and baryon spectra with one common two-body interaction. A Hamiltonian calibrated to ground-state mesons leaves systematic baryon mass residuals, largest in the light-quark sector and decreasing toward heavier flavors. We show that a short-range, color-spin-dependent connected three-quark interaction substantially reduces this incompatibility. Mass-scaled finite-range profiles yield high-accuracy baryon spectra, whereas flavor-independent common-range profiles do not remove the residual flavor pattern. The result is tested on additional ground-state baryons outside the calibration set and through meson--baryon compatibility analyses across several alternative quark-model Hamiltonians. We also benchmark radial and orbital excitations to identify the regime in which a static compact valence Hamiltonian remains reliable, and provide explicit color-spin matrix elements for two- and three-body operators in baryons and multiquark configurations. Within the tested valence-space representations, the results indicate that a mass-dependent short-range connected three-quark interaction provides the missing contribution required for a consistent simultaneous description of meson and baryon ground-state spectra.
item.dc:creator: Jongheon Baek, Aaron Park, Emiko Hiyama, Sungsik Noh, Hyeongock Yun, Kyong Chol Han, Su Houng Lee

item.title: Probing Dirac Dark Matter in Composite Higgs Models with Xenon and Argon targets
item.description: arXiv:2608.24791v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recent advancements in direct detection (DD) experiments stimulate the investigation of the interactions of dark matter (DM) with nucleons and nuclei. In the framework of Composite Higgs Models (CHMs) the lightest Dirac composite particle (LDCP) can be stable composing a significant fraction \xi of the observed DM relic abundance. We consider the elastic scattering of the LDCP on nucleons as well as on xenon (Xe) and argon (Ar) nuclei within the CHMs in which the LDCP magnetic moment, its mass and its coupling to the Higgs doublet are suppressed by an approximate U(1) symmetry. The LDCP with non-zero magnetic dipole moment can result in a substantial enhancement of the differential event rate in the DD experiments at low recoil energies of nuclei. Assuming \xi\ge 0.1, we identify the region of the parameter space where such enhancement may be potentially observable. In addition we specify some observables that can be useful in discriminating between the DM fermions with non-zero magnetic moment and other types of dark matter particles which don't have similar electromagnetic properties.
item.dc:creator: M. G. Belyakova, R. Nevzorov

item.title: Strangeness, entropy, and chemical non-equilibrium from p+p to Pb+Pb: the $K^+/\pi^+$ horn on the system-size axis
item.description: arXiv:2608.28189v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The maximum ("horn") of the $\langle K^+\rangle/\langle\pi^+\rangle$ excitation function in central Pb+Pb collisions near $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}} = 7.6$ GeV is interpreted as the competition between strangeness production and the faster rise of entropy production at the onset of deconfinement. Statistical hadronization analyses by Letessier, Rafelski, and collaborators have shown that the horn is described quantitatively only if the light-quark phase-space occupancy $\gamma_q$ is free, with $\gamma_q$ near the pion condensation limit from 30$A$ GeV upward. We carry this analysis along the system-size axis provided by NA61/SHINE (p+p, Be+Be, Ar+Sc, preliminary Xe+La) and NA49 (Pb+Pb). Our main new result is the first non-equilibrium analysis, to our knowledge, of the Be+Be and Ar+Sc $4\pi$ multiplicities, published in 2021 and 2024: in Ar+Sc, chemical equilibrium of light quarks ($\gamma_q = 1$) is disfavored, but through the $K^+/K^-$ asymmetry rather than the pion yields, while the Be+Be data do not discriminate. For central Pb+Pb, our fits to the final NA49 data confirm the earlier result, most robustly at 30$A$-80$A$ GeV; the preference rests on the excess of produced hadrons per net baryon and on the Bose-Einstein enhancement of pions. Decomposing $\langle K^+\rangle/\langle\pi^+\rangle$ into strangeness and pion yields per wounded nucleon, we find that the step between Be+Be and Ar+Sc is carried by a doubling of strangeness per participant, whereas the horn appears only in Pb+Pb, where the pion yield per participant is suppressed at 20$A$-40$A$ GeV. Parton-hadron transport (PHSD) reproduces the Pb+Pb horn but predicts one also in Ar+Sc and Xe+La, where none is observed.
item.dc:creator: Neeraj, Amal Sarkar

item.title: Fermion mass hierarchies in a three-generation Clifford model
item.description: arXiv:2608.29259v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We examine whether an algebraic model of three fermion generations based on the complex Clifford algebra $\mathbb C\ell(10)$, in which an $S_3$ family symmetry relates the generations, can reproduce the observed mass hierarchies of the charged leptons and down quarks. Taking the internal Gram matrix as the fermion kinetic metric, we show that the original Yukawa interaction, with complex coefficients, gives precisely those ordered mass triples $0\leq m_1\leq m_2\leq m_3$ for which $m_3\leq m_1+2m_2$. This restriction excludes the observed hierarchies in both sectors and persists when the right-acting Higgs operator is allowed to range over the full Clifford algebra. This obstruction motivates a second Yukawa contraction in which a projector, constructed from the difference between an internal charge operator and its family average, acts from the left. The resulting interaction preserves the gauge and family symmetries and uses the same three Higgs doublets. With both contractions present, there is a fixed coupling ratio at which the two successive mass ratios in a single sector become arbitrarily large along a real vacuum path. Separately, a rational interval calculation establishes that one real Higgs vacuum, with different coupling ratios in the two sectors, reproduces the chosen running masses of the charged leptons and down quarks. A softly broken three-doublet potential realises this vacuum as a global minimum at tree level. The additional neutral scalars have flavour-changing couplings, and their exchange at a common mass of $2000\,\mathrm{TeV}$ satisfies the neutral-meson mixing criterion and the $\mu\to3e$ contact-interaction test considered here.
item.dc:creator: Ye Zhou, Niels Gresnigt

item.title: Analysis of the two-body strong decays of the hidden-charm pentaquark states in QCD sum rules
item.description: arXiv:2609.02537v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In the present work, we study the two-body strong decays of the hidden-charm pentaquark states with the quark content $uudc\bar c$ and the quantum numbers $I(J^P)=\frac{1}{2}(\frac{1}{2}^-)$ in the framework of the three-point QCD sum rules. The initial pentaquark states are described by four local diquark-diquark-antiquark type interpolating currents with definite isospin. We construct the three-point correlation functions for the decay channels $P_c\to \eta_c p$, $J/\psi p$, $\Lambda_c\bar D$, $\Lambda_c\bar D^{*}$ and $\Sigma_c\bar D$, and derive the corresponding QCD sum rules for the strong coupling constants. At the hadron side, the correlation functions are expressed in terms of the hadron masses, pole residues, decay constants and strong coupling constants. At the QCD side, they are calculated by carrying out the operator product expansion with the full quark propagators, where the vacuum condensates up to dimension 10 are taken into account. After matching the two representations and performing the double Borel transformations, we extract the strong coupling constants from the selected Lorentz structures. With the obtained coupling constants, we evaluate the partial decay widths and discuss the possible assignments of the corresponding pentaquark states. The numerical results indicate that two of the compact hidden-charm pentaquark states can be related to the $P_c(4312)$ and $P_c(4457)$, respectively, while the other two lower-mass states may be regarded as possible hidden-charm pentaquark candidates to be searched for in future experiments. The present results may be useful for identifying the hidden-charm pentaquark states in future experiments.
item.dc:creator: Zi-Hao Chen, Han-Xiong Huang, Jie Lu, Xiao-Song Yang, Zhi-Gang Wang, Guo-Liang Yu

item.title: Measuring Dual-Superconductor Length Scales in the QCD Vacuum at HERA
item.description: arXiv:2609.28700v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In the dual-superconductor picture, the QCD vacuum behaves like a superconductor for chromoelectric fields, with characteristic penetration and coherence lengths. These scales have so far been studied primarily through lattice calculations of static flux tubes. We show that they are also imprinted on exclusive diffraction, where the transverse profile of a gluonic hotspot reflects the response of the vacuum to a localised colour source. Using the Clem vortex profile, we fit all 104 H1 and ZEUS measurements of exclusive $J/\psi$ photoproduction and find $\chi^2/{\rm ndf}=0.72$, the penetration depth $\lambda=0.19(2)~{\rm fm}$, the hotspot core size $\xi_v=0.087(14)~{\rm fm}$, and the Ginzburg--Landau parameter $\kappa=2.6(8)$, placing the effective vacuum description in the type-II regime. The corresponding vector mass $1/\lambda=1.03(11)~{\rm GeV}$ agrees with the lattice gluelump mass, and the extracted parameters reproduce the QCD string tension.
item.dc:creator: Tobias Toll, Nahid Vasim

item.title: Fractal phase structure of QCD under imaginary rotation
item.description: arXiv:2610.07779v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that in hot QCD rotating at an imaginary angular velocity $\tilde\Omega_I$, the angular velocity selects not only the temperature of the bulk but whether charge conjugation $C$ is broken there. For QCD at temperature $T$ and imaginary quark chemical potential $\theta$, with $\tilde\Omega_I/2\pi=p/q$ in lowest terms, the bulk far from the rotation axis is in the same thermal equilibrium state as nonrotating QCD at temperature $T/q$ and imaginary quark chemical potential $\theta'=q\theta+\pi(p+q+1)$; this follows from the Euclidean boundary conditions and locality alone, and holds nonperturbatively whenever the equivalent nonrotating system has a finite correlation length. Consequently, even at zero quark chemical potential, the bulk is placed at the Roberge-Weiss (RW) point whenever $p$ and $q$ are both odd, and $C$ is spontaneously broken there for $T>qT_{\rm RW}$, with $T_{\rm RW}$ the RW endpoint temperature. The bulks at $\tilde\Omega_I=2\pi/3$ and $4\pi/3$, for example, are both at temperature $T/3$, yet only the former can break $C$. The set of imaginary angular velocities at which $C$ is broken has a fractal structure: raising $T$ adds rationals of ever larger denominator. At irrational $\tilde\Omega_I/2\pi$ the bulk corresponds to zero-temperature QCD at any $T$ and remains confined.
item.dc:creator: Rin Takada

item.title: Production of the weakly bound $T_{cc}^+$ state combining the coalescence model with its mass spectrum
item.description: arXiv:2610.29392v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the production of the doubly charmed molecular state $T_{cc}^+$ within the coalescence model. The formation probability is evaluated with the Wigner distribution function. In contrast to previous studies, which usually adopt a Gaussian wave function, we obtain the molecular wave function by numerically solving the coupled-channel Schr\"odinger equation with the one-boson-exchange potential fitted to the mass spectrum of $T_{cc}^+$. The resulting wave function is the universal form of a weakly bound $S$-wave molecule in momentum space (a Yukawa-type exponential in coordinate space), dressed by the dipole form factor of the OBE interaction, and is thus more suitable for such a state. As the input of the coalescence model, we use the transverse-momentum distributions of the constituent $D$ and $D^*$ mesons fitted to the ALICE and LHCb data, and also generated by PYTHIA for comparison. We compute the transverse-momentum distributions of $T_{cc}^+$ in $pp$ and Pb-Pb collisions. The two collision systems differ in which part of the wave function is probed: for the extended Pb--Pb source the universal pure-Lorentzian form suffices, whereas for the compact $pp$ source the short-distance part of the wave function, captured by the dipole form factor, becomes relevant. These results provide a theoretical reference for future experimental measurements of $T_{cc}^+$.
item.dc:creator: Ao Wang, Yu-Shan Ren, Zhi Yang

item.title: Inelastic Kinetic Decoupling in WIMP Leptogenesis: A Minimal $Z_4$ Model
item.description: arXiv:2610.38531v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a minimal $Z_4$-symmetric extension of the Standard Model in which a singlet Dirac fermion $\chi$ constitutes dark matter, whose annihilations generate a lepton asymmetry through WIMP leptogenesis. Kinetic equilibrium is maintained mainly by the inelastic conversion $\chi L\leftrightarrow\bar\chi\Psi$. Compared with the near elastic regime, a sizable mass gap suppresses the conversion rate more rapidly as the Universe cools. This naturally drives kinetic decoupling to earlier times, even away from resonance. Starting from the full inelastic collision operator, we derive an effective momentum transfer rate for kinetic decoupling. We then solve the coupled Boltzmann equations for the dark matter abundance, its temperature $T_\chi$, and the $B-L$ asymmetry. Early kinetic decoupling can significantly modify the relic abundance, although near resonance this modification can be reduced by annihilation-induced heating. The $B-L$ asymmetry can be affected when asymmetry production overlaps with a substantial departure from kinetic equilibrium. In our scan, the largest deviations occur mainly for $x_{\rm lep}\gtrsim x_{\rm cd}$. After imposing our constraints, asymmetry production typically ends before chemical decoupling, leaving the final asymmetry essentially unchanged. For indirect detection, we generate the photon spectrum with Pythia and evaluate the Fermi-LAT dwarf spheroidal likelihood.
item.dc:creator: An Liu, Hong-Hao Zhang

item.title: RG evolution of the $B$-meson LCDA and radiative jet function at three loops
item.description: arXiv:2611.18206v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We calculate the three-loop evolution kernel of the light-cone distribution amplitude of the $B$ meson, together with the radiative jet function in the leptonic radiative decay $B^-\to\gamma\ell^-\bar\nu$ for the first time. Representing the light-cone distribution amplitude as the discontinuity of a matrix element containing an inverse differential operator, we compute the partonic matrix element in momentum space with a novel method of infrared subtraction. We show that its infrared singularities are governed by the same anomalous dimension as that of the heavy-light quark form factor, so that they can be subtracted without introducing any infrared regulator, thereby preserving gauge invariance and avoiding additional complexity in the Feynman integrals. Based on the renormalization-group invariance of the factorization theorem, we derive the renormalization factor of the radiative jet function, and confirm that it removes all divergences of the bare three-loop radiative jet function. Our results enable renormalization-group improved predictions for exclusive $B$ decays at next-to-next-to-next-to-leading order.
item.dc:creator: Ze Long Liu, Guang Tang, Zhe-Yu Wang

item.title: Perspective on Proton Transversity Distribution Functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.23577v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Using available information on proton tensor charges and constraints from perturbative quantum chromodynamics (QCD), Ansaetze are introduced for hadron-scale in-proton valence-quark transversity distributions functions (DFs). The concept of a QCD effective charge, which defines an evolution scheme for collinear parton distribution and fragmentation functions that is all-orders exact, is then used to deliver predictions for the $x$-dependence of these DFs at the scale $\zeta_{2} = 2\,$GeV. Although the approach is largely algebraic, its predictions remain viable after comparisons with results obtained using computationally intensive methods. Thus, given the scarcity of data that can today be used for inference of proton transversity DFs, it may be worth using the results herein to inform and constrain related experiments and phenomenological fits.
item.dc:creator: Ke-Xin Zeng, Peng Cheng, Yang Yu, Daniele Binosi, Craig D. Roberts

item.title: Search for Heavy Charged Higgs Bosons in Boosted Top and Bottom Quark Final States at a 1.4 TeV Future Lepton Collider
item.description: arXiv:2611.24241v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The discovery potential for heavy charged Higgs bosons $H^\pm$ decaying into a top-bottom quark pair is investigated at a future $e^+e^-$ collider operating at $\sqrt{s}=1.4~\mathrm{TeV}$. The study considers charged Higgs masses between 200 and 600 GeV within all four Yukawa types of the two-Higgs-doublet model (2HDM). The boosted $tb$ final state is explored using complementary cut-based and machine-learning analyses based on boosted decision trees (BDT). The expected signal significance and sensitivity contours in the $(m_{H^\pm},\tan\beta)$ plane are obtained for each Yukawa type. The resulting sensitivity extends to regions of the 2HDM parameter space beyond the projected reach of the High-Luminosity LHC (HL-LHC), demonstrating the complementary potential of a future high-energy lepton collider to probe heavy charged Higgs bosons.
item.dc:creator: Majid Hashemi

item.title: $X(2370)$ without exceptionalism from reanalyzing $J/\psi \to \gamma + 3P$ data
item.description: arXiv:2611.24372v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Motivated by recent BESIII claims that $X(2370)$ is a pseudoscalar glueball candidate, we reanalyze several radiative $J/\psi$ decays into three pseudoscalars, $J/\psi\to\gamma PPP$, with emphasis on the $X(2370)$ region. A simultaneous analysis of the three invariant-mass projections in $J/\psi\to\gamma K_S^0K_S^0\eta^\prime$, including the pseudoscalar states $X(1835)$, $X(2120)$, $\eta(2225)$, $X(2370)$, $X(2500)$, and $\eta_c$, reproduces the observed dip near $2.2~\mathrm{GeV}$ and the enhancement near $2.4~\mathrm{GeV}$ through coherent interference, without invoking the additional broad $X(2800)$ component employed in the BESIII partial-wave analysis. We further analyze $J/\psi\to\gamma\pi^0\pi^0\eta$ and $J/\psi\to\gamma K_S^0K_S^0\pi^0$ by including both pseudoscalar and axial-vector contributions, and show that multiple excited meson states collectively describe the data. The absence of a prominent $X(2370)$ signal in the $K^*(892)$ region can be understood from differing orbital angular-momentum requirements rather than flavor-singlet suppression alone. Our results indicate that $X(2370)$ is not exceptional compared with the other reported pseudoscalar states in this mass region. Therefore, interpreting $X(2370)$ as a glueball-dominated state should be treated with caution.
item.dc:creator: Tian-Cai Peng, Xiang Liu

item.title: Chiral QCD phase in equilibrium with Hadron Gas and the location of the critical point
item.description: arXiv:1812.07006v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a description of the equation of state of QCD matter with restored chiral symmetry, which is in thermal and chemical equilibrium with the hadronic phase. The hadron gas is described with thermodynamically consistent volume corrections. The chiral phase is composed of a set of few quark condensates, each of which corresponds to a family of hadrons with specific quark content. On the boundary between the two phases we apply the requirement of conservation of particle numbers per family. We use lattice calculations for temperatures below the transition curve to determine hadronic volumes. We find that the pion system plays decisive role in the shift of the transition from higher order (crossover) to first order. For four volume models and five hadron sets we calculate the location of the critical point as function of critical temperature $T_c$ at vanishing baryon density. Among other acceptable solutions, if we additionally impose the equality between the densities of quarks contained in mesons and baryons, we find a critical point residing in the interval of baryon chemical potential $\mu_B \simeq$ 234-279 MeV and of temperature $T \simeq$ 148-156 MeV. We propose as signal of approach to the critical point the determination of the chiral pion mass through experimentally measured pion multiplicities in heavy-ion collisions.
item.dc:creator: N. G. Antoniou, F. K. Diakonos, A. S. Kapoyannis

item.title: CMB constraints on $U(1)$ axion warm inflation
item.description: arXiv:2507.17438v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this work, we propose a model of warm inflation driven by axion-like particles interacting with $U(1)$ gauge fields, with implications for the early universe's thermal evolution. By extending traditional warm inflation models, we introduce a dissipation mechanism through the thermal fluctuations of electromagnetic fields, leading to a non-trivial back-reaction on the inflaton's dynamics. Our results are consistent with CMB observations, even for a natural sub-Plankian Axion decay constant $f\leq M_{\rm Pl}$. We present precise constraints on the model's free parameters, using CAMB and CosmoMC codes. These findings offer new insights into the thermal history of the universe and the nature of inflationary dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Asma Alaei, Sukannya Bhattacharya, Vahid Kamali

item.title: Non-Abelian Casimir energy in the Curci-Ferrari model through a functional approach
item.description: arXiv:2509.07256v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Using functional integral methods, we investigate the non-Abelian Casimir energy in the Curci-Ferrari model, which offers an effective description of the infrared regime of Yang-Mills theory. We consider a 3+1D (resp.\ 2+1D) system of two infinite parallel plates (resp.\ wires) at a fixed distance from each other, with either perfect magnetic conductor (PMC) or perfect electric conductor (PEC) boundary conditions. Imposing the boundary conditions directly in the functional integral by the introduction of suitable auxiliary fields that act as Lagrange multipliers, we obtain a boundary effective action that captures the dynamics of this system. The Casimir energy is then computed both directly from the functional integral and via the energy-momentum tensor, providing equivalent results. We find that the Casimir energy for PEC and PMC conditions differs by a constant factor, which can be traced back to a van Dam--Veltman--Zakharov-like discontinuity (both in 3+1D and 2+1D). Lastly, we show that our analytical results are compatible with a variety of recent numerical lattice simulations of the non-perturbative Yang-Mills Casimir energy, in which a novel non-perturbative mass scale emerges.
item.dc:creator: David Dudal, Philipe De Fabritiis, Sebbe Stouten

item.title: Effects of dark dipole radiation on eccentric supermassive black hole binary inspirals
item.description: arXiv:2510.08514v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The final-parsec problem has long posed a central challenge in understanding the merger of supermassive black hole binaries. In this paper, we investigate a scenario in which a dark scalar or vector field is sourced by eccentric binaries, leading to accelerated mergers through additional dipole radiation, and thereby extending the range of masses for which the binary can merge within a Hubble time. The Newtonian-order radiation fluxes from an eccentric charged Keplerian binary are derived using general results for localized periodic sources in flat spacetime. We find that dipole radiation, although insufficient to fully resolve the final-parsec problem, can alter the low-frequency spectrum of the stochastic gravitational wave background from supermassive black hole binary inspirals. We construct a simplified model for the spectrum and perform a Bayesian analysis using the current pulsar timing array data.
item.dc:creator: Mu-Chun Chen, Yan Cao

item.title: How Bright in Gravitational Waves are Millisecond Pulsars for the Galactic Center GeV Gamma-Ray Excess? A Systematic Study and Implications for Dark Matter
item.description: arXiv:2511.15793v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The existence of dark matter (DM) is supported by various macroscopic observations, but its microscopic nature remains elusive. The Galactic Center GeV gamma-ray excess (GCE) has been a leading candidate signal for particle DM annihilation. However, an unresolved population of millisecond pulsars (MSPs) in the bulge provides the alternative explanation for the excess. Identifying these MSPs in electromagnetic bands is difficult due to source confusion, pulse broadening, and extinction. Gravitational waves (GWs) provide a complementary probe: a steadily rotating, non-axisymmetric MSP emits a nearly monochromatic GW signal in the sensitive band of ground-based detectors, with amplitude set by its ellipticity. In this work, we systematically investigate the GW emission from the MSP population proposed to explain the GCE and its detectability with current and future detectors. We consider three major scenarios for the origin of ellipticity and model the population properties of these MSPs. We also consider both isolated MSPs and MSPs in binary systems, as well as Doppler effects in the detection. We find that while the signal is below the reach of current interferometers, next-generation detectors such as the Einstein Telescope (ET) and Cosmic Explorer (CE) may detect a fraction of those MSPs, offering a novel test of the MSP interpretation of the GCE. Future directed searches toward the Galactic Center may either uncover this long-sought MSP population or place stringent constraints on bulge MSP properties. Continued improvements in detector sensitivity will provide increasingly stringent tests of the MSP interpretation, with growing power to distinguish between the astrophysical and DM interpretations of the GCE.
item.dc:creator: Ming-Yu Lei, Bei Zhou, Xiaoyuan Huang

item.title: Solving the Domain Wall Problem: Primordial Magnetic Fields as a Dynamical Solution
item.description: arXiv:2511.22949v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: To prevent overclosing the Universe, stable domain walls must decay-a problem typically addressed by breaking the Peccei-Quinn symmetry with a bias term. In this Letter, we present a novel mechanism in which a helical primordial magnetic field provides a spatially inhomogeneous Chern-Simons source that drives the axion field. We validate this mechanism through three-dimensional lattice simulations of the evolving domain-wall network, demonstrating its efficacy in inducing decay. Our quantitative analysis reveals that the correlation length of the primordial magnetic field is a crucial determinant of the decay rate of the network and the properties of the emitted axions and gravitational waves. In particular, the axion emitted from the decaying domain-wall network can contribute to the dark matter abundance, and the associated gravitational-wave signal lies in the frequency range probed by pulsar timing array experiments.
item.dc:creator: Zizhuo Zhao, Yuefeng Di, Ligong Bian, Jing Shu

item.title: Toward Neutrino and Dark Matter Detection with Ancient Minerals: TEM Study of Heavy-Ion Tracks in Olivine
item.description: arXiv:2604.09732v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Solar, supernova, and atmospheric neutrinos, and possibly weakly interacting massive particle (WIMP) dark matter, have been interacting in the Earth beneath our feet for billions of years. The ''paleo-detector'' technique seeks to detect and characterize the induced crystalline defects from these events, in particular from energetic nuclear recoils, which in some minerals can be preserved on these timescales. Such defects can manifest as nuclear recoil tracks, on the order of a few nanometers wide and extending up to hundreds of microns in length, which can be detected with nanoscale-resolution microscopy. In order to test the feasibility of the paleo-detector technique and to study the formation and morphology of track defects in promising mineral candidates like olivine, we use ion irradiation to artificially implant tracks to effectively mimic astrophysical particle interactions. We present a study of heavy-ion track width as a function of depth, which we relate to ion energy, in an olivine crystal irradiated with 15 MeV Au$^{+5}$ using scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM). Unlike previous studies, which measure tracks at the surface of the irradiated sample, we instead take measurements at various target depths via focused ion-beam sectioning of the irradiated sample. No etching techniques are used to enhance the tracks. In addition, we provide a comparison to predictions from simulations using SRIM software and previous results with a variety of ion species and energies. Notably, we find that a significant change in track continuity across the energy range studied (0.4-12.9 MeV) is indicative of the transition between electronic and nuclear stopping power dominance, consistent with the simulations' predictions. Overall, the tracks produced in olivine indicate that this mineral is an attractive candidate for paleo-detection, with robust track creation at the MeV scale.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Calabrese-Day, Emilie LaVoie-Ingram, Kathryn Ream, Hannah Ross, Joshua Spitz, Patrick Stengel, Kai Sun, Alexander Takla

item.title: Characterizing entanglement dynamics in QED scattering processes
item.description: arXiv:2604.10136v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the entanglement among helicity degrees of freedom in quantum electrodynamics (QED) scattering processes at fixed momentum, modeled as quantum maps whose spectral structure determines the associated entanglement dynamics. We show that, for fermion-fermion scatterings, parity invariance preserves maximal entanglement and generically leads to entanglement saturation under iterations of the maps. The structure of the maps also provides an accurate description of the entanglement dynamics in processes involving both fermions and photons.
item.dc:creator: Massimo Blasone, Silvio De Siena, Gaetano Lambiase, Bruno Micciola, Kyrylo Simonov

item.title: Anomalous Transport from Effective Field Theory
item.description: arXiv:2605.15968v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A systematic study of chiral effects is presented using an Effective Field Theory framework. By integrating out a massive Dirac fermion at finite temperature in presence of vector and axial background fields, the currents and their anomalies are computed from the path-integral. Chiral effects previously considered separately naturally arise in a unified computation, including new mass corrections. The link between each anomalous transport effect and the anomalies is clearly established, beyond the identification of their coefficients. In particular, we can appreciate how these effects are sourced by the anomalous nature of the theory even in configurations where the anomaly itself vanishes. The consistent and covariant anomalies are both encapsulated in master formulae for the currents which result from a careful treatment of the regularisation. It is finally found that, at finite temperature, the physical currents cannot be inferred simply from the Chern-Simons terms whose divergence reproduce the chiral anomalies.
item.dc:creator: R\'emy Larue, Amaury Marchon, J\'er\'emie Quevillon, Diego Saviot

item.title: Polarized Nuclear DVCS at the EIC
item.description: arXiv:2606.11491v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Electron-Ion Collider (EIC) will enable a series of measurements at unprecedented energies and luminosities, providing new opportunities to investigate the microscopic structure of nucleons and nuclei at small $x_B$. Exclusive processes such as Deeply Virtual Compton Scattering (DVCS) offer unique access to the three-dimensional structure of hadrons through Generalized Parton Distributions (GPDs), while polarized electron and ion beams further enable detailed studies of spin-dependent structure. A model for coherent DVCS on polarized $^3$Heis developed and applied to simulations of for $9\times166$-GeV $e^3$He collisions at the EIC. Using this framework, the statistical precision achievable is estimated for measurements of beam-spin asymmetries and for the extraction of the Compton Form Factors (CFFs) $\mathcal H_{^3\mathrm{He}}$ and $\tilde{\mathcal H}_{^3\mathrm{He}}$. Early EIC data are found to enable precise differential measurements of the unpolarized CFF $\mathcal H_{^3\mathrm{He}}$ and to provide significant constraints on its real and imaginary components. By contrast, meaningful constraints on the polarized CFF $\tilde{\mathcal H}_{^3\mathrm{He}}$ require substantially larger integrated luminosities. The kinematics of the recoil $^3$He nucleus are also examined, and the advanced far-forward detector capabilities at the EIC required to tag the intact nucleus and perform fully exclusive measurements of coherent nuclear DVCS are discussed.
item.dc:creator: Jackson R. Pybus, Xuan Li, Liliet Calero-Diaz

item.title: Articulating Assumptions in AI-Generated Scientific Analyses through Task Decomposition
item.description: arXiv:2607.05762v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Scientific results produced by LLM generated analysis code must be understandable and reproducible. However, uncertainty can arise at different stages of the process, both in the original natural language specification and in the generated implementation. As a result, even executable code may not provide a clear understanding of which quantities are being computed or which assumptions determine the final results. To address this challenge, we introduce quantity grounded semantic differencing, a multi-agent framework for analyzing and comparing scientific programs generated by LLMs. The framework assigns code generation, execution, tracing, and validation to separate agents, allowing it to reconstruct how key output quantities are produced and to identify differences between the intended analysis and the implemented code. We also introduce a module that inspects ambiguities in the initial user instruction and suggests alternative rewrites before code generation. Its modular design enables application to different scientific domains by replacing domain specific resources while preserving the same workflow. We validate the framework on representative collider physics analyses. The results demonstrate that the modular task decomposition enhances both transparency and reliability relative to the previous single prompt approach, while enabling substantially smaller models to execute the complete workflow.
item.dc:creator: Ahmed Hammad, Mihoko Nojiri

item.title: Forward deuteron breakup on carbon and hydrogen: Coulomb effects and the high-momentum excess
item.description: arXiv:2607.17222v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate whether recoil and the Coulomb interaction can explain the excess of protons at large longitudinal momenta in $^{12}$C(d,p)X. We calculate the spectrum in the Glauber--Sitenko model, retaining longitudinal momentum transfer and the transverse momentum of the detected proton. At a beam momentum of 9.1 GeV/c and a longitudinal proton momentum of 0.325 GeV/c in the rest frame of the incident deuteron, the invariant differential cross section with recoil is 2.8--3.6 mb/GeV$^2$, against 18.5 mb/GeV$^2$ in the published spectrum. The Coulomb correction to the channel sum is small in this region. Near the main peak at zero proton angle, the coherent cross section rises by 4--12%, while the sum of coherent breakup and neutron removal changes by less than 0.2% in the transverse approximation. At 3.5 GeV/c we compare the calculated carbon and hydrogen spectra with Sitnik's measurements for several transverse cuts. The effects considered here do not account for the high-momentum excess. Further observables are needed to establish whether it has a quark origin.
item.dc:creator: Yaroslav D. Krivenko-Emetov, Boris I. Sydorenko

item.title: Matrix Multiverses Meet Multiple Mythologies
item.description: arXiv:2608.08972v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a model in which asymptotically de Sitter universes of various types, and de Sitter (dS) radii $R_n$, live in the interiors of black holes in a maximally entropic flat $p = \rho$ Friedmann-Robertson-Walker universe. These dS universes clearly have many quantum states. We argue that they decay and equilibrate with the maximal entropy universe on time scales of order $\alpha_n R_n {\rm ln} (R_n /\delta_n)$, where $\alpha_n$ are model-dependent dimensionless constants and $\delta_n$ are the initial distances between the shell, satisfying the Israel junction conditions, and the dS horizon. These are time-scales as viewed by a detector following a trajectory far from the would-be cosmological horizon. These times are all exponentially shorter than dS recurrence times, which have no meaning in this model. It is impossible for a detector inside one of the dS universes to determine whether it is actually part of such a structure. This model could be used as the basis for claiming that certain constants of nature or cosmological initial conditions were chosen to have mathematically unnatural values because other values could not lead to any form of intelligent life.
item.dc:creator: Sidan A, Tom Banks, Willy Fischler

item.title: Relic Neutrinos Probing Small Scale Primordial Non-Gaussianity
item.description: arXiv:2609.34324v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Relic neutrinos retain a record of electromagnetic entropy production after neutrino decoupling, probing primordial modes erased from the primary CMB. We derive the cubic photon number source from acoustic damping and its leading folded sensitive bispectrum window, with neutrino decoupling, thermalization, and acoustic coherence combined in a single response kernel. For excited initial states, this kernel filters the physical folded profile and yields a sharpness dependent transmission condition, directly connecting small scale primordial non-Gaussianity to relic neutrino capture rates.
item.dc:creator: Suraj Gavhale, Shin'ichi Nojiri, Sergei D. Odintsov, Oem Trivedi

item.title: Massive de Sitter Correlators as Finite Mellin-Barnes Integrals
item.description: arXiv:2610.10921v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Using the Mellin-Barnes representation of de Sitter propagators, we reduce tree-level heavy-particle exchange to finite integrals that converge at physical kinematics on mass-independent contours, and one-loop diagrams to the same integrand times a flat-space momentum factor. We compute the complete one-loop triangle at general masses, with its collider signal in closed form to all orders in the squeezed-limit expansion, and give the triple-exchange bispectrum at arbitrary heavy masses as a double series that converges at every physical shape. The loop reduction also applies at strong mixing.
item.dc:creator: Amara McCune

item.title: Pretraining on boosted boson decays for polarization tagging of hadronic $W$ bosons
item.description: arXiv:2610.27346v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Longitudinally polarized weak bosons probe the unitarization of vector-boson scattering. At large boosts, longitudinal and transverse $W$ bosons produce jets with the same mass and two-prong structure, distinguished only by the decay angle. Longitudinal bosons are rare in $W$+jet events at these large boosts. We ask where the polarization information of a boosted $W$ boson lies and how much a tagger can recover. Requiring both decay quarks within the jet truncates the decay-angle distribution at an edge set by $m/(p_T R)$, which, as we show, bounds any hadronic polarization tagger. Within this acceptance, the decay angle carries nearly all the polarization information of a jet in $W$+jet events. Whether pretraining retains the decay angle is not obvious, so we pretrain a point-edge transformer on $10^7$ unpolarized boosted-boson, top-quark and QCD jets and fine-tune it with $10^3$ to $5\times10^4$ labeled jets per class. With the fewest labels, a boosted decision tree on substructure observables performs best; with the most labels, the strongest networks come within 0.003 in AUC of the ideal decay-angle tagger. Pretraining saves a factor of about two to three in labels, and our boson pretraining improves on a generic one by a few thousandths in AUC, more with frozen transformer blocks. Student networks with a few hundred times fewer parameters, distilled with unlabeled jets, match their teacher. More information lies outside the jet. The production angle, reconstructed with the recoiling jet, improves every tagger. In diboson production and vector-boson scattering at matrix-element level, the production kinematics carry more information than the decay angles of both bosons. Trading the generality of a jet tagger for an event-level tagger trained on the process thus brings large gains, which measurements of longitudinal vector-boson scattering could exploit.
item.dc:creator: Saptaparna Bhattacharya

item.title: Precision measurement of coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering at a nuclear reactor by CONUS+
item.description: arXiv:2610.37318v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We report the most precise measurement to date of coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering (CE$\nu$NS) from reactor antineutrinos, using the CONUS+ germanium detectors at the Leibstadt nuclear power plant. With an exposure of 1296 kg$\cdot$days reactor-on, a blind likelihood analysis yields a signal with high statistical significance, corresponding to $1565 \pm 155$ CE$\nu$NS events, in agreement with the Standard Model expectation of $1701 \pm 198$ events within 0.5 $\sigma$. The flux-averaged cross section is $(0.57 \pm 0.09)\times10^{-40}$ cm$^{2}$, and the weak mixing angle at a momentum transfer of about 10 MeV is $\sin^2\theta_W = 0.226 \pm 0.022$.

item.title: Nonperturbative lattice simulation of the nucleation rate in thermal first-order phase transitions
item.description: arXiv:2611.18794v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a nonperturbative lattice study of vacuum decay through bubble nucleation in a three-dimensional real scalar field theory at finite temperature. The vacuum decay rate is computed by combining an expanded-ensemble multicanonical hybrid Monte Carlo approach, which samples the critical bubble configurations, with real-time Langevin dynamics, which follows the subsequent bubble evolution. We extrapolate the nucleation rate to the continuum limit and compare it with the corresponding one-loop perturbative prediction, finding a discrepancy of about 6.6%.
item.dc:creator: Jing Zhou, Ligong Bian

item.title: Lie-Poisson Formulation of Dissipative Spin Hydrodynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.22615v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Covariance and the second law cannot fix how fluid flow couples to spin, since reversible couplings produce no entropy. We show that the spin commutation relations and the Poincar\'e algebra fix these couplings. Reversibly, a flow exerts no torque on the spin: its magnitude per particle is conserved, its direction is Fermi--Walker transported, and spin--shear couplings reflect a deforming triad. The magnitude changes only through higher multipoles, as in spinor condensates, or dissipation, whose first-order spin--shear coupling reorients the spin away from the vorticity above a critical shear rate.
item.dc:creator: Zi-Hao Liu, Mei Huang

item.title: Classification of Chern-Simons Couplings and Deformed Pull-Backs on D-Branes
item.description: arXiv:2611.26374v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish a geometric framework for classifying higher-derivative Ramond-Ramond (RR) couplings on Dp-branes, focusing on the complete scattering amplitude of a closed-string RR state, a gauge field, and two transverse scalars. The low-energy expansion reveals infinite massless poles and local interaction terms that are beyond standard Myers and Taylor expansions. We propose a higher-class deformation of the pullback using mixed Chern-Simons transgression operators to address these complexities. We also propose a generalized class Chern character and three conjectures: (i) the finite dimensionality of independent couplings at fixed derivative order, (ii) the representation of all-order mixed RR-gauge-scalar interactions through finitely many effective even forms, and (iii) the generation of higher-derivative contact terms from finitely many primitive tensor structures. Our framework provides a systematic mathematical foundation for reconstructing D-brane effective actions and exploring their underlying geometric and cohomological structures. We also introduce a higher-class pullback operator \( P_{\infty} \) and mixed transgression operators \( \mathcal{T}_{\infty} \), emphasizing amplitude-derived pole residues and local contact terms as key physical data. This formalism distinguishes admissible tensor structures, presenting characteristic-form aspects as conjectures alongside their validity and their constraints.
item.dc:creator: Armin Hatefi, Ehsan Hatefi
